artigo.texto: Trump ameaça proibir data centers de americanos fora do país. Regulamentação do Redata no Brasil empaca. Presidente dos EUA informou que estaria disposto a impor um 'imposto enorme' para impedir que empresas norte-americanas construam data centers fora do país. Aqui no Brasil, a regulamentação do Redata empaca e ninguém explica o porquê. O presidente Donald Trump ameaçou tributar empresas norte-americanas que construírem data centers no exterior — uma medida que, segundo ele, ajudaria o setor de Inteligência Artificial do país a manter-se à frente da China. “Não vamos permitir que nossas empresas construam data centers fora do nosso país”, disse Trump em uma coletiva de imprensa na Casa Branca, na semana passada, após sua viagem à Ásia, informou a Reuters. Ele declarou que imporia um “imposto enorme” às empresas caso elas construam data centers no exterior. Trump não forneceu detalhes sobre como planeja aplicar esses impostos às empresas de tecnologia e de IA que apoiaram sua presidência. A medida, se vingar, afeta muito o mercado brasileiro. Empresas como a Equinix, Digital Realty, AWS, Google e outras teriam de rever seus projetos em plena época de debate sobre soberania digital. As declarações mais recentes de Trump seguem outras iniciativas relacionadas à IA, incluindo uma determinação para que grandes empresas de tecnologia construam suas próprias usinas de energia, bem como um plano de ação voltado a garantir a supremacia na área de IA. Segundo a agência de notícias, Trump tem defendido enfaticamente a construção de data centers nos Estados Unidos, embora estados e comunidades em todo o país tenham manifestado resistência devido à demanda por eletricidade, aos custos de serviços públicos e a outros impactos locais. Na semana passada, o Departamento de Comércio dos EUA tomou medidas para restringir a exportação de chips avançados de IA para diversos países do Sudeste Asiático — parte de um esforço mais amplo para impedir que a China obtenha essa tecnologia por meio de terceiros países. E que também afetou diretamente o Brasil. Enquanto isso, a prometida regulamentação do Redata, para depois da volta do presidente Lula ao Brasil da viagem à Ásia. Aqui o texto empacou na Casa Civil e não há explicações sobre o porquê.

artigo.texto: As entregas do Denza B5 no Brasil - SUV de luxo que puxou Boeing 747 por mais de 1 km sobre duas rodas - devem se normalizar em janeiro de 2027, segundo Werner Schaal, diretor da marca. O executivo afirmou à reportagem que 5 mil unidades do veículo já estão a bordo de navio a caminho do nosso País. A previsão é que cheguem entre o fim de dezembro e o início de janeiro. O tamanho da remessa dá certa ideia da escala da reposição. Os 5 mil carros em trânsito superam os cerca de 3,8 mil B5 emplacados no país de janeiro a outubro de 2026. Só em outubro, foram 577 unidades, o suficiente para manter o SUV na liderança mensal do segmento de luxo pela quinta vez consecutiva. O BMW X1, seu principal rival, registrou 405 emplacamentos no mesmo período. Já no acumulado do ano, o modelo ainda segue na liderança, com 3.949 licenciamentos. De acordo com Schaal, o volume de unidades importadas do B5 é suficiente para suprir o número de vendas estipulado pela Denza para o SUV em 2027. E, claro, para buscar a liderança no segmento. No entanto, vale salientar que a marca já prepara a produção local do modelo para o próximo ano - como confirmado por Alexandre Baldy, vice-presidente sênior da companhia para o Brasil. Primeiro vêm os navios, depois entra Camaçari Enquanto a Denza reforça o estoque com carros importados da China, a BYD prepara, conforme comentamos, a produção do B5 na Bahia. Segundo a fabricante, o SUV começará a ser fabricado em Camaçari ao decorrer de 2027. Alexandre Baldy, vice-presidente sênior da BYD Brasil, confirmou, inclusive, que ele será o primeiro modelo da marca de luxo a sair da linha baiana. Janeiro, portanto, é a previsão para regularizar as entregas com o lote importado. O mês de estreia do B5 nacional segue em aberto. A fábrica, que hoje monta veículos com kits de peças vindos da China, está na fase final de implantação das áreas de estamparia e soldagem. Com elas, a BYD poderá produzir peças de carroceria e soldá-las na própria unidade. O investimento no complexo de Camaçari já ultrapassa R$ 11 bilhões. Quanto custa o Denza B5? Hoje, o B5 custa R$ 405 mil na versão GL e R$ 505 mil na GS. Ambas combinam um motor 1.5 turbo a gasolina com dois elétricos, um em cada eixo. São 687 cv e 77,5 kgfm de torque para levar o SUV de zero a 100 km/h em 4,8 segundos, segundo a Denza. A marca ainda não divulgou se o modelo passará por reajustes assim que iniciada a montagem na Bahia. Uma das diferenças entre as versões aparece fora do asfalto. A GS traz suspensão hidráulica adaptativa, que permite elevar o vão livre do solo a 31 cm, ante 22 cm na GL. Na cabine, a versão de entrada já oferece bancos dianteiros com ventilação e massagem. A GS acrescenta revestimento de couro Nappa, aquecimento nas duas fileiras e uma tela de 12,3 polegadas para o passageiro da frente. Carregando ofertas...

artigo.texto: CBRE Group Eyes Mid-Double-Digit Growth as Data Center and Infrastructure Demand Builds CBRE Group CBRE expects to grow in the “mid-double digits” next year and finish the current year strongly, Chairman, CEO and President Bob Sulentic said at JPMorgan’s Ultimate Services Investor Conference. Sulentic said the company’s outlook remains largely consistent with what it articulated on its most recent earnings call. He also pointed to growth in infrastructure services and recurring businesses as factors that have made CBRE less dependent on the commercial real estate capital markets cycle. Infrastructure and data center demand CBRE has shifted its business mix toward what it calls resilient businesses, which generate recurring revenue and are countercyclical or acyclical, Sulentic said. He said those businesses now represent 60% of the company’s business. Infrastructure work spans all four of CBRE’s reporting segments and includes assignments involving data centers, energy, water and transportation. Sulentic said the company is ahead of its previously discussed goal of reaching $10 billion in infrastructure-related revenue by 2030. On its latest earnings call, CBRE discussed having $7 billion in that type of revenue next year, he said. In data centers, CBRE oversees construction, installs network infrastructure and provides mechanical, electrical and plumbing project services, as well as ongoing facilities management. Sulentic said refitting existing data centers is also a significant opportunity as operators seek more computing capacity. Sulentic said the midterm election results could slow new data center development for a time, but he does not expect a notable impact on CBRE’s business. He cited demand that has exceeded the company’s capacity, its expanding overseas presence and work on existing facilities. CBRE’s Direct Line acquisition added U.S. data center network infrastructure capabilities, while Onnec provides similar services outside the United States, including in the Nordics and Malaysia, Sulentic said. Facilities growth and capital markets Sulentic expects CBRE’s traditional facilities management business to grow at a low-teens rate overall. He projected mid-teens or better growth for its local facilities management business, compared with high-single-digit to potentially double-digit growth in large corporate outsourcing. Capital markets remain important to CBRE, but their effect on the company’s overall growth trajectory is smaller than it was a decade ago, Sulentic said. Uncertainty about interest rates has recently caused some participants to move to the sidelines, he said. CBRE expects capital markets-related activity in commercial real estate to remain “flattish” through at least the middle of next year. Sulentic said greater certainty about rates could encourage more trading in the second half, though he does not expect rates to fall substantially. In leasing, CBRE expects double-digit growth in the fourth quarter and mid- to high-single-digit growth next year, led by industrial leasing. Sulentic said office leasing has also been strong, though limited availability of Class A space in the United States has created challenges. Acquisitions and buybacks Sulentic said strategic acquisitions remain CBRE’s preferred use of capital, with opportunities in technical services, facilities management, critical infrastructure and project management. The company also supports its real estate investment businesses through co-investments and direct investments. CBRE continues to repurchase shares when it believes they trade below intrinsic value, Sulentic said. He said buybacks have likely been the company’s largest use of capital over the past few years, while adding that CBRE has not been capital constrained in pursuing acquisitions and real estate investments. About CBRE Group CBRE CBRE Group, Inc. is a commercial real estate services and investment company serving property owners, occupiers, investors and developers. Its services include property leasing and sales, property and facilities management, project management, valuation, consulting and commercial real estate financing. The company also provides real estate investment management and development services. Through its global operations, CBRE serves clients across a range of property types and markets, including offices, industrial facilities, retail properties and data centers. artigo.texto: SAN DIEGO (KGTV) — The battle over data centers has entered a new era. Several local cities have banned the facilities, while others have passed moratoriums. However, Cal State University San Marcos Political Science Professor Larry Gerston said a local ban can only go so far — and comes as Trump is insisting the facilities be built in America. Gerston told ABC 10News he's writing a book called Breaking Point. "It's about the issues that are driving concerns in America." Gerston said. Gerston said one of the main concerns, on both sides, has to do with data centers. "And so the question is, of course, if it's worth having it, what are the gains from having it versus the losses from having it? That's the conversation. That's the national conversation. That's the state conversation. That's the local conversation." Gerston said. That local conversation on large-scale data centers has been dominated by resistance. It's been about a month since the City of San Diego temporarily halted the development of data centers, in response to a potential project at the Naval Information Warfare Systems Command — or NAVWAR — site in the Midway District. Escondido also put a pause on their development. Poway banned them outright. At the federal level, it's a different story. "We're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country. We're not going to allow that to happen," Trump said in a press conference last Friday after meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Gerston said, "In other words, that leads to a bit of a controversy given resistance that we have — and therein lies the problem." Part of the problem is a loophole, per se, in the system. Local bans have little to no influence on federal land. For example, since the NAVWAR site is owned by the U.S. Navy, a city ban alone wouldn't stop a data center from being built there. Gerston said public opinion could provide the real power. "I think you can expect to see Congress act on that. You can expect to see it go all the way to the President's desk, and at that point, as they say, where the rubber meets the road, we'll have to see just what the President says." Gerston said. artigo.texto: Franklin leaders move forward with proposed rules that would limit where data centers can be built. Here’s what we know The city’s proposed zoning update would limit where data centers can be built. A final vote is scheduled for December 8. What This Story Is About - Franklin’s Board of Mayor and Aldermen has advanced a zoning update that would require new data centers to be at least 2,640 feet, or half a mile, from residential lots. Why It Matters - The proposal would limit where new data centers could be built. City planning staff said existing data centers would retain the ability to expand, though the meeting discussion did not detail the rules governing those expansions. What Happens Next - The board unanimously approved the update Tuesday. A third and final reading is scheduled for December 8, with a proposed effective date of Jan. 1, 2027. FRANKLIN, Tenn. (WSMV) - New data centers in Franklin would have to be at least half a mile from residential lots under a zoning update advanced by city leaders Tuesday. The Board of Mayor and Aldermen unanimously approved the proposed changes after a public hearing. The update would also limit the zoning districts where new data centers are allowed. The changes are not final. A third and final reading is scheduled for December 8, with a proposed effective date of Jan. 1, 2027, according to city planning staff. Board debates distance from homes Under the proposal, new data centers would remain allowed in planned development and light industrial districts, subject to a 2,640-foot buffer from residential lots, planning staff said. The proposal would remove data centers as a principal use in several other zoning districts. A city planning representative said staff initially proposed a 1,320-foot, or quarter-mile, buffer. Following discussion at a board work session, the Planning Commission amended the proposal to double that distance. During Tuesday’s meeting, an alderman questioned whether a half-mile buffer was necessary and proposed returning to the quarter-mile distance. The amendment did not receive a second, so the half-mile requirement remained in the proposal the board approved. Planning staff said the buffer would apply even when a new data center is proposed as part of a planned development. Staff also said existing data centers would be able to expand, but did not detail the rules governing expansions during the meeting discussion. Other business City Administrator Eric Stuckey told the board that Franklin had settled a consolidated federal lawsuit concerning the 2023 Franklin Pride Festival. He said the settlement includes $20,000 in damages for each of three plaintiffs and $80,000 in attorney fees, all to be paid by the city’s insurer. Settlement of more than $100K reached in lawsuit over Middle TN police interaction at pride festival A separate lawsuit remains scheduled for trial on Jan. 12, 2027, Stuckey said. artigo.texto: Carlos Wizard amplia investimentos em Portugal com expansão da Help Battery Empresário aposta em modelo de hubs logísticos para serviço de atendimento automotivo 24 horas e prevê chegar a 80 unidades no mercado Português O empresário Carlos Wizard está ampliando seus investimentos na Europa com uma nova frente de atuação no setor de serviços em Portugal. No início deste ano, Wizard associou-se a um grupo de empresários brasileiros radicados no país para impulsionar a expansão da Help Battery, empresa que atua no atendimento automotivo emergencial. Com sede em Braga e operação há mais de seis anos, a Help Battery oferece atendimento 24 horas a motoristas que enfrentam problemas relacionados à bateria de seus veículos. A proposta é levar o serviço ao cliente de forma ágil, com uma estrutura operacional apoiada por hubs logísticos distribuídos em diferentes regiões. O modelo de expansão adotado para o negócio difere do sistema de franquias que marca a trajetória empresarial de Carlos Wizard. Na Help Battery, a operação central concentra atividades como estratégia comercial, expansão, marketing, atendimento ao cliente, cobrança e gestão da entrega dos produtos e serviços. O investidor, por sua vez, torna-se proprietário de um hub logístico responsável pelo armazenamento das baterias utilizadas na região atendida. Segundo a empresa, a estrutura foi concebida para operar sem a necessidade de uma equipe própria de funcionários no hub, já que a gestão operacional é centralizada pela matriz. Expansão em Portugal Com investimento inicial acessível a partir de 70 mil euros, o candidato interessado no projeto pode ter operações em cidades como Lisboa, Coimbra e Porto, além da expansão gradual para outras regiões de Portugal. A expectativa de Wizard é alcançar 80 hubs de atendimento no país e, posteriormente, avaliar a entrada da Help Battery em outros mercados europeus. Além da oportunidade de investimento, o projeto é apresentado como uma alternativa para brasileiros que consideram estabelecer negócios e residência no exterior. De acordo com Wizard, os investidores recebem suporte na preparação da documentação necessária para o processo de imigração, obtenção do visto adequado à condição de investidor e regularização comercial em Portugal. "Após as eleições, cresceu significativamente o número de famílias interessadas em imigrar para os Estados Unidos, Canadá e vários países da Europa. Essa é uma opção para quem busca diversificação em seus investimentos ou até mesmo a imigração para um novo país", afirma Carlos Wizard. Para o empresário, a entrada em novos mercados também faz parte de uma estratégia de diversificação e busca por oportunidades além dos segmentos em que tradicionalmente atua. "O sucesso do passado não garante o sucesso do futuro. De tempos em tempos, é necessário analisar e considerar novos modelos de negócios e novos mercados", conclui Wizard.

artigo.texto: Transmissoras de energia sinalizam que não vão participar dos leilões de baterias marcados para os próximos dias 2 e 4 de dezembro, a despeito de terem se engajado há anos em estudos e projetos pioneiros de baterias instaladas na Rede Básica. O motivo é a possibilidade de terem de compartilhar com os consumidores a receita proveniente dos sistemas de armazenamento, para fins de modicidade tarifária. A Taesa já anunciou que não vai participar do certame, mesmo após ter cadastrado diversos projetos para a disputa. A diretora Financeira da empresa, Catia Pereira, explicou à Coluna que o principal motivo da desistência é a insegurança regulatória e citou dúvidas relacionadas à “modicidade tarifária”. “Pensando em disciplina de capital, pensando em ter clareza sobre essa questão regulatória que vem para as baterias, dado que estamos em um setor regulado e muito previsível, temos um cuidado maior, então decidimos tirar o pé desse leilão e continuar estudando, continuar contribuindo com essa discussão regulatória, mas não participando”, afirmou. Já a Isa Energia, detentora do primeiro projeto de baterias do Brasil, instalado junto à subestação Registro, no Estado de São Paulo, afirmou, também no início do mês, que analisava a potencial participação no leilão de baterias “com cautela”. A diretora executiva de Finanças, Relações com Investidores e Desenvolvimento de Negócios da companhia, Silvia Wada, também justificou a prudência adotada pela existência de “incertezas” sobre o certame, incluindo a questão da modicidade tarifária e rateio do encargo que custeará os sistemas contratados no leilão. Pela lei em vigor, o custo será arcado exclusivamente pelas geradoras, em um formato ainda sujeito a regulamentação da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel). A regra desagradou as geradoras, que tentam alterar a norma no Congresso e entraram na Justiça para tentar suspender o leilão e tornar a regra inconstitucional. Durante videoconferência com analistas e investidores, Wada afirmou que o potencial compartilhamento de receita poderia reduzir a competição no certame, uma vez que inviabilizaria a participação das transmissoras. Regulação O tema do compartilhamento de receitas não consta no edital do leilão, mas chegou a ser comentado em reunião de diretoria da Aneel, durante a deliberação sobre esses documentos. O assunto veio à tona após a Taesa fazer uma consulta ao regulador sobre a necessidade de alteração do Estatuto Social da companhia caso viesse a participar do certame e obtivesse outorga independente na condição de armazenador. As áreas técnicas da agência indicaram que a transmissora poderia disputar o leilão e constituir uma Sociedade de Propósito Específico (SPE) sob controle direto, mas teria a captura de parte da receita para modicidade tarifária para os usuários conectados no segmento de transmissão. Durante a reunião da Aneel, um representante da Taesa criticou a orientação e defendeu que a participação da transmissora deveria ser em “igualdade de condições, em benefício da isonomia e da livre concorrência”, portanto sem a captura de receitas do novo segmento, mas como atividade segregada. “Aqui a transmissora não está prestando serviços de engenharia dentro de seu contrato de concessão, mas sim como empreendedor único e independente de armazenador de bateria, para participar desse leilão, com objetivo de ter uma outorga de armazenamento”, argumentou Rafael Janiques, advogado que falou em nome da empresa. Ele lembrou que já existe no mercado estrutura de modelo de negócios em que um mesmo CNPJ opera concessões de transmissão e separadamente usinas de geração ou concessões de distribuição, sem compartilhamento de receitas, e citou empresas como Axia, Copel e EDP. O procurador geral junto à Aneel, Eduardo Ramalho, explicou que a procuradoria qualificou a atividade de armazenamento como conexa aos contratos de concessão existentes, o que permitiria o compartilhamento de receitas. Já o diretor relator do processo sobre o edital do leilão, Gentil Nogueira, avaliou que o regulador não controla todas as formas possíveis de participação de uma transmissora no certame e em que medida algum ativo poderia ser compartilhado, por isso não poderia fazer uma análise genérica sobre o tema. Com isso, a questão ficou em aberto. Com a palavra Procurada pela reportagem, a Associação Brasileira das Empresas de Transmissão de Energia Elétrica (Abrate) disse entender que o compartilhamento para a modicidade tarifária só se justifica quando há aproveitamento de ativos já remunerados pelos consumidores via Receita Anual Permitida (RAP). “Esse pressuposto não se aplica a projetos de armazenamento estruturados de forma autônoma - com outorga própria, patrimônio, financiamento e contabilidade segregados, investimentos integralmente novos, riscos assumidos pelo investidor e sem uso de bens reversíveis ou recursos da RAP”, disse, por meio de nota. Diante da indefinição, a entidade apresentou uma carta à Aneel solicitando à Secretaria de Leilões e às áreas técnicas da agência uma manifestação conclusiva que sinalizasse para a não aplicação do mecanismo de captura de receitas para a modicidade tarifária nos casos de Sistemas de Armazenamento estruturados com outorga própria, patrimônio, financiamento e contabilidade segregados, sem utilização de bens reversíveis, recursos das concessionárias de transmissão ou custos imputados a essas concessões. No entanto, até o momento nenhuma comunicação oficial foi divulgada pelas autoridades setoriais. artigo.texto: Finanças Petrobras planeja investir em minerais críticos e baterias para armazenamento de energia Estatal inclui exploração, mineração e refino dessas matérias-primas em seu plano de negócios, além de montagem de células de bateria, com previsão de entrada no setor a partir de 2029 Petrobras planeja entrar nos segmentos de minerais críticos e de baterias de grande escala para armazenamento de energia. Ao divulgar, esta semana, seu plano de negócios para os próximos cinco anos, que prevê investimentos de US$ 122 bilhões, a estatal apontou estas como possíveis áreas de atuação. A petrolífera tem uma joint venture com a Lightsource, que se inscreveu para participar dos leilões de baterias de energia previstos para dezembro. A Petrobras afirmou identificar uma demanda crescente por energia de operações de data centers, do setor de transportes e também da indústria. A Petrobras está aumentando em cerca de 4% os gastos totais com a transição energética, para US$ 13,5 bilhões, destinando mais recursos à descarbonização de suas operações e à pesquisa e desenvolvimento de tecnologias de baixo carbono, mesmo com a redução dos investimentos planejados em energias renováveis e outras fontes de baixa emissão. A estatal brasileira está buscando desenvolver tecnologias de baterias em um momento em que grandes petroleiras, como BP, Shell e Equinor, reduziram os investimentos na transição energética para concentrar os aportes nos negócios mais rentáveis de petróleo e gás. A Petrobras pretende priorizar minerais que ofereçam as maiores sinergias com seus negócios de energia, especialmente aqueles utilizados em baterias. As atividades potenciais incluem exploração, mineração, refino e montagem de células de bateria, com previsão de entrada no setor a partir de 2029. Por enquanto, a empresa utilizará sua “expertise em pesquisa e desenvolvimento” para acompanhar “a evolução desses segmentos”, afirmou William Vella Nozaki, diretor executivo de Transição Energética e Sustentabilidade da Petrobras, em entrevista coletiva. A empresa também vê um cenário favorável de políticas públicas para essa expansão. O governo Lula busca aproveitar os vastos recursos minerais do Brasil para impulsionar atividades de processamento e manufatura, em vez de se concentrar apenas na exportação de matérias-primas, abrindo oportunidades para a Petrobras em diferentes etapas da cadeia produtiva. A Petrobras não toma decisões de negócios “em resposta a solicitações do governo”, e os minerais estratégicos “continuam sendo uma iniciativa de pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação”, afirmou Nozaki. artigo.texto: Residents of Dade County gathered in Trenton, Georgia, Monday night, just one week after the county’s Industrial Development Authority withdrew a letter of intent with Masterworks Atlanta, LLC for a proposed data center. The pitch caught many off guard at the November 5th County Commission meeting where a potential 90-day moratorium on data centers was scheduled to be introduced. That announcement led to an uproar from the crowd and caused the commission to push the 90-day moratorium discussion to its next meeting on December 3rd. Still, protesters express their frustration with a lack of communication and transparency. “We're very uncomfortable with the data centers because of the non-disclosure agreement, all the smoke and mirrors that's going on behind the scenes. Yeah, the local authorities say they're going to put a moratorium, but there's a lot more going on,” said Rob Rush, a resident and former congressional candidate. Protest organizer Carter McCormick says they are also concerned by the existing lack of regulations. “Recently our IDA has rescinded their letter of intent to sell to Masterworks. So while that proposal has kind of been taken off the docket, we still remain as a county very vulnerable to hyperscale development, as we don't have any zoning laws here in the county. So as it stands now, there is absolutely nothing that can stop a hyperscale data center from coming in next door,” McCormick says. McCormick says their demonstration Monday night is a push to be a part of the conversation and for more transparency moving forward. “I think it's important for our community leaders to see that we are not divided on this issue. This isn't red, Blue; it's something that's bringing us together in this community, all across the political aisle, and we just want to be protected,” McCormick said. Commissioner Melissa Bradford, who introduced the moratorium, told Local 3 in a statement that she agrees that transparency is key. “I think transparency is the key to county government. I want to see work being done in open meetings. I would like to have ordinances and policy in place before these types of industry come in to our county! I am tried of back tracking and being on a limited schedule to protect the citizens of these type of business. I want to be proactive,” Bradford said in the statement.

artigo.texto: Siga Reset no Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. Siga Reset no Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. O Brasil antecipou para 2026 a exportação de créditos de carbono para aproveitar uma janela de oportunidade do Corsia, sistema de compensação de emissões da aviação internacional. No entanto, ao excluir os créditos de conservação de programas jurisdicionais, o Brasil vai ficar de fora desse mercado. A avaliação é de Natália Renteria, diretora de Brasil da Silvania, empresa suíça de soluções baseadas na natureza que atua com programas estaduais de geração de créditos. “As duas metodologias que foram escolhidas não vão atender o programa e nós vamos ficar de fora do Corsia se isso não for revisto”, disse Renteria no ClimaCorp, evento promovido pelo Reset nesta segunda-feira (23), com patrocínio de Itaú, MBRF e Santander, apoio da Vale e apoio institucional da BR Partners. Segundo a especialista, as duas atividades autorizadas pelo governo – de restauração florestal e de metano de resíduos – não atendem aos critérios do Corsia. Segundo ela, os créditos jurisdicionais de conservação florestal (JREDD) são os únicos brasileiros capazes de atender a essa demanda. Para serem aceitos pelo Corsia, esses créditos precisam se tornar ITMOs (Resultados de Mitigação Transferidos Internacionalmente), instrumento criado pelo Artigo 6 do Acordo de Paris para que países cooperem entre si no cumprimento de suas metas climáticas, as NDCs. Cada um equivale a uma tonelada de CO2 equivalente evitada ou removida da atmosfera, e pode ser vendido a outro país ou usado em programas como o Corsia. O governo anunciou no começo do mês as metodologias que serão aceitas na primeira fase de exportação de ITMOs, além do limite que poderá ser vendido para fora: 50 milhões de toneladas até 2030 e 100 milhões entre 2031 e 2035. A exclusão de créditos de conservação (o que inclui os de projetos, os REDD+, e os jurisdicionais, os JREDD) provocou uma reação dos Estados que possuem programas jurisdicionais, que pressionam o governo para rever essa decisão. As metodologias e os limites de volumes foram anunciados, mas a resolução para consolidar as regras e o funcionamento das transações ainda não foi publicada. O texto final aguarda aprovação da Casa Civil. Arquitetura de demanda Para Renteria, o mercado internacional entrou na fase de “arquitetura da demanda”. Cada comprador define seus próprios critérios, e nenhum tipo de crédito atende a todos. O país precisa, segundo ela, de uma estratégia de ITMOs que case volume, preço e prazo de entrega com cada mercado. “É importante que os critérios [para ITMOs] permitam a entrada de créditos diferentes, porque valores diferentes vão ser praticados em momentos diferentes e o uso vai ser regulado pelo próprio mercado. Um crédito só não vai atender à demanda de todo o mercado”, afirma Renteria. O Corsia é hoje o maior desses mercados de demanda regulada. As companhias aéreas precisarão compensar, de forma obrigatória, parte de suas emissões entre 2027 e 2029, na segunda fase do Corsia. A demanda estimada é de meio bilhão de créditos, segundo Mary Grady, presidente do conselho da Associação Internacional de Comércio de Emissões (Ieta, na sigla em inglês) e diretora executiva da certificadora ART Trees. A especialista aponta problemas nas duas metodologias escolhidas. No caso da restauração, os créditos brasileiros vêm de projetos, e apenas remoções em nível de programas jurisdicionais são elegíveis ao Corsia, modalidade que o Brasil não pratica, indica Renteria. Já no caso dos créditos de resíduos, os problemas são de preço e volume. Segundo a diretora da Silvania, esses créditos são negociados com valor acima do que se paga no Corsia, entre US$ 13 e US$ 20 por tonelada. “A empresa aérea tem obrigação de compra. Se ela não comprar no Brasil, vai comprar em outro país. O dinheiro sai do Brasil”, afirma Renteria. “A gente não está competindo com crédito, estamos competindo com outros países, porque esse mercado é global.” Justificativas O governo deu quatro justificativas para não incluir os créditos de conservação neste primeiro momento: (1) o preço que poderia ser derrubado com o excesso de oferta, uma vez que os créditos de conservação são os mais comuns no país e de maior volume; (2) garantir que haja créditos para o cumprimento da NDC; (3) a harmonização da contabilidade retirar projetos privados da contabilidade dos jurisdicionais e (4) dúvidas sobre a consulta a povos indígenas e comunidades tradicionais. Renteria argumenta que um possível excesso de oferta e a possibilidade de derrubar preço podem ser resolvidos pelos próprios limites autorizados pelo governo, que pode calibrar o volume. Em relação à harmonização entre as contabilidades de carbono de projetos e a nacional, ela argumenta que a divergência se aplica apenas a projetos privados, e não aos programas jurisdicionais, cuja contabilização é compatível com a nacional. Quanto à consulta a povos indígenas e comunidades tradicionais, Renteria defende que eventuais problemas identificados em um programa específico não sejam generalizados para os demais. Segundo ela, essas questões estão sendo tratadas e resolvidas. “Generalizar questões pontuais ligadas a um programa, e não a outro, que estão sendo resolvidas não faz sentido. Temos que ser os primeiros a defender o nosso crédito jurisdicional, habilitá-lo para atender a uma demanda que já existe e trazer financiamento para o Brasil.” Renteria também argumenta que o reconhecimento do governo influencia a demanda de compradores internacionais. Os créditos que não forem admitidos como ITMOs poderão ser comercializados no mercado voluntário, como é hoje. “Se o próprio governo não reconhece valor naquele crédito, como o comprador corporativo vai ver valor?”, pergunta.

artigo.texto: In a narrow decision, McHenry County officials have approved a pair of battery storage projects that will operate at solar farms – the first such projects the County Board has voted on since new state requirements went into place over the summer. The county cannot adopt stricter requirements than state law on battery storage projects, a provision that was outlined in a new state clean energy law that took effect in June. An earlier, similar state law that applied to solar farms sparked backlash from county officials who say it has forced them into the position of having to approve solar farms under legal pressure that they’d already rejected. The McHenry County Board approved the two battery storage plants in a pair of 10-8 votes at its November meeting, and board members voted the same way on both of them. Both battery storage plants are located in Coral Township in the southwestern part of the county and are near each other. They are proposed to be about 5 megawatts each. Battery storage plants store electricity from the grid and then release it when electricity is in high demand. While it may be the first direct vote the County Board has taken on battery storage plants in recent months, residents in Prairie Grove have been opposed to a proposed battery storage plant off Behan Road. Pivot Energy is the developer behind both of the Coral Township projects. Brittney Krebsbach, a representative with the company, told the board the company will continue to work with all parties involved and will uphold its commitments to safety and community accountability. She said the company is looking forward to working with current and incoming board members. Board member Terri Greeno, R-Crystal Lake, said she was voting no because local fire officials have raised concerns about the projects. County documents indicate Union Fire Protection District officials had raised concerns to the Zoning Board of Appeals about battery storage projects. After the votes, County Board member Mike Shorten, R-Crystal Lake, said in a statement the county kept battery storage out of solar developments before this year but state law has since overridden the county’s ability to decide that. “Springfield’s takeover of local zoning for solar, wind and industrial battery facilities is a massive overstep,” Shorten said in a statement. “State law has taken this decision away from the people who live here. That’s why I voted no on both battery projects.” Shorten said he also has concerns about fire safety at large lithium battery sites, as well as about flooding, saying one of the sites has about 30 acres in a 100-year floodplain. “Putting industrial batteries in a floodplain is exactly the kind of decision that should be made locally, not dictated by Springfield,” Shorten said. Shorten said state and federal authorities “should speed up small modular nuclear reactors and invest in fusion power, which can deliver safe, reliable, low-cost energy.” Greeno was unsuccessful in her reelection bid this fall and is among six County Board members who are leaving after their terms expire in December. Shorten, who is also the elected Nunda Township supervisor, is up for reelection to the County Board in 2028. The new board is due to be seated Dec. 7.

artigo.texto: Greenvolt constrói projetos solar de 100 MW e de armazenamento de energia em baterias de 200 MWh nos EUA - A Greenvolt Power deu início à construção do projeto Alamogordo, um ambicioso híbrido de energia renovável situado no condado de Otero, no Novo México. - O projeto combina 100 MWac de energia solar com um sistema de armazenamento de 50 MW / 200 MWh, representando um investimento superior a 120 milhões de dólares. - A conclusão do projeto está prevista para o verão de 2028, com a criação de mais de 370 postos de trabalho, beneficiando a comunidade local. Conteúdo Este resumo foi criado com recurso a inteligência artificial. Embora esta tecnologia tenha sido concebida para ser útil e precisa, pode conter erros ou não captar todas as nuances importantes do artigo. Feedback Se consideras que o resumo não está claro ou não reflete bem o conteúdo, envia o teu feedback. A tua opinião é importante para ajudar a melhorar esta funcionalidade! Partilhar A Greenvolt iniciou a construção de um projeto solar de 100 MWac, combinado com um sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias de 50 MW / 200 MWh, no Novo México, EUA, representando um investimento superior a 120 milhões de dólares (aproximadamente 109 milhões de euros). A Greenvolt Power, área de negócio do Grupo Greenvolt dedicada a projetos de energias renováveis de grande escala, iniciou a construção do projeto Alamogordo, um projeto híbrido de energia renovável localizado no condado de Otero, no Novo México, Estados Unidos, foi divulgado em comunicado. Segundo a mesma fonte, combinando 100 MWac de produção solar com um sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) de 50 MW / 200 MWh, o projeto representa um investimento superior a 120 milhões de dólares (aproximadamente 109 milhões de euros) e constitui um passo importante no desenvolvimento contínuo da atividade da Greenvolt nos Estados Unidos. Prevê-se que o projeto esteja totalmente concluído até ao verão de 2028, tornando-se o maior projeto combinado de energia solar e armazenamento de energia em baterias da Greenvolt nos Estados Unidos. O sistema de baterias, instalado no mesmo local, terá capacidade para armazenar eletricidade durante um período máximo de quatro horas, permitindo disponibilizar posteriormente a energia produzida durante os períodos de maior produção solar, maximizando o seu valor e promovendo uma utilização mais flexível das energias renováveis. O projeto assegurou um Contrato de Aquisição de Energia (PPA) de longo prazo para a venda da eletricidade produzida, proporcionando à Greenvolt receitas contratualizadas e previsibilidade financeira durante um período alargado. Este projeto integra o portefólio global de projetos da Greenvolt nos Estados Unidos, ponderado pela respetiva probabilidade de concretização, que totaliza atualmente 341 MW de energia eólica, 686 MW de energia solar e 212 MW de capacidade de armazenamento de energia em baterias, abrangendo diferentes fases de desenvolvimento. Neste mercado, a Greenvolt tem vindo a reforçar a sua estratégia de investimento, explorando oportunidades tanto no desenvolvimento de novos projetos como no repowering (modernização e otimização de instalações existentes). João Manso Neto, CEO do Grupo Greenvolt, afirma: “os Estados Unidos assumirão um papel cada vez mais importante na concretização do plano de negócios do Grupo. Temos vindo a analisar atentamente as oportunidades de investimento, tendo em consideração os fundamentos de cada projeto e a sua capacidade para criar valor sustentável, tanto para o Grupo como para as comunidades onde os nossos projetos estão localizados”. Weronika Nowak, CEO da Greenvolt Power USA, afirma: “é particularmente gratificante ver o projeto Alamogordo avançar, uma vez que demonstra aquilo que a Greenvolt faz melhor: transformar um projeto, desde a sua conceção até à sua concretização. Este marco é o resultado de uma colaboração extraordinária entre as nossas equipas, parceiros, empreiteiros e entidades locais”. Os trabalhos de engenharia, aprovisionamento e construção (EPC) estão a ser assegurados pela CJR Renewables, responsável pelas instalações solares e pelo sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias, e pela Dashiell Corporation, responsável pela subestação e pelo parque de corte e manobra do projeto. A Greenvolt Power está também a gerir a conceção e construção das infraestruturas de ligação do projeto à rede elétrica. Durante a fase de construção, prevê-se a criação de mais de 370 postos de trabalho, proporcionando benefícios económicos adicionais e de longo prazo à comunidade local, bem como contribuindo para o cumprimento das metas de energias renováveis do Novo México para 2040.

artigo.texto: Concerns have arisen that Native American artifacts or human remains could be found at the site selected for the University of Michigan’s planned data center in partnership with Los Alamos National Laboratory. The State Historic Preservation Office warned the University the $1.25 billion data center’s proposed location is “highly archaeologically sensitive” due to its proximity to the Huron River. The University chose a 144-acre site along Textile Road — a historic Native American trail — as the preferred location for the data center in August, citing its access to technical infrastructure and separation from residential areas. On Oct.16, the United Tribes of Michigan adopted a resolution opposing the data center development without proper consultation and safeguards. The University issued a statement on Oct. 30 in response, claiming a background search found “no evidence of archeological artifacts or culturally-sensitive materials.” In the resolution, UTM considered the historic Native American usage of the land and burial sites adjacent to the property. They further expressed concern over the project’s potential impacts on tribal cultural resources. “United Tribes of Michigan expresses its support of Ypsilanti Township as it seeks to guide this potential development including its demand that consultation with the Tribes be conducted prior to any development,” the resolution reads. In an interview with The Michigan Daily, Ypsilanti Township attorney Doug Winters said the township is unsatisfied with the University’s practices. Although the regents approved of a Community Investment Resolution, which calls on the University to implement a Community Partnership Program with Ypsilanti Township, Winters criticized it as an attempt to distract from environmental racism. “They picked this area in Washtenaw County because we have the largest percentage of Black and brown (people),” Winters said. “We have less access to healthcare and educational opportunities. We don’t have generational wealth, and there’s a reason why they chose this part of the township: because they did not expect to have this kind of a pushback.” Winters said he does not trust the University to conduct a careful archaeological assessment before beginning construction on the center. “They’re not going to do the right thing unless they’re forced to do it,” Winters said. “We intend to make sure they’re held accountable on that issue.” In an interview with The Daily, LSA senior Calvin Stineman, a former intern at the University’s Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act Office, said the data center’s scientific advancements should not come at the cost of disrespecting Native American culture. “These sorts of precedents — along with all other data centers being built in places around the country — undermine the community’s sentiments and show how we are moving backward as a university and a society in terms of our respect for human and environmental agency,” Stineman said. Winters said Ypsilanti Township is working to build partnerships with UTM to oppose the data center. Winters was invited to Traverse City by UTM to share Ypsilanti Township’s resolution against the data center. The Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act mandates federally-funded institutions consult with Tribal Nations about the repatriation of Native American cultural items and human remains. “They are required by federal and state law to do an archeological investigation whenever there’s evidence of Indigenous artifacts and burial grounds,” Winters said. “They have to consult with the Native American tribes before they go forward with any type of activity on that property.” In an interview with The Daily, University alum Vidhya Aravind, member of local advocacy group Stop the Data Center, criticized the University’s lack of transparent communication with the community regarding the data center. “While I do wish for a more open channel between the University and its impacted communities more broadly, here it seems unlikely that anything we would have said would have killed this project, which the community clearly and unanimously doesn’t want,” Aravind said. “They’re not communicating with us because they know it’s bad too.” Daily Staff Reporter Mercy Wisecup can be reached at wisecup@umich.edu.

artigo.texto: Utica Common Council discusses BESS legislation at committee meeting Alexis Manore | Staff writer | AManore@RNYmedia.com Alexis Manore Staff writer Author facebook Author linkedin Author twitter Author email Nov 24, 2026 5 hrs ago 0 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Utica City Hall Sentinel photo by John Clifford Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save UTICA — The Utica Common Council discussed proposed legislation to regulate battery energy storage systems (BESS) at a Monday, Nov. 23 Committee of the Whole meeting. The council currently has a moratorium on BESS in Utica, having passed several extensions, with the most recent extension set to expire Saturday, Dec. 5. The council’s next regular meeting is Wednesday, Dec. 2. At the Nov. 23 meeting, the councilors reviewed legislation that Assistant Corporation Counsel Stephanie DiGiorgio prepared. The legislation split BESS into three tiers: one for smaller systems that would be allowed, one for larger systems that would require site plan approval from the Planning Board, and the third for large-scale systems, which would only be allowed in industrial and mixed-use industrial zones, and would require a special use permit. After discussion, the councilors decided that large-scale systems should not be allowed at all, and talked about further regulating second-tier systems. The councilors decided to call for a special meeting on Monday, Nov. 30 to introduce its BESS legislation, before introducing it at its Dec. 2 meeting. Check back at ursentinel.com for more information. artigo.texto: It’s the Roaring 2020’s for the HPC-AI Data Center Industry, But It Comes with Costs Key Highlights - Overall HPC spending grew nearly 17% in 2025 to more than $70 billion, with cloud usage up nearly 30%. - The combined on-premises and cloud market for HPC and AI-for-science servers is projected to approach $140 billion by 2030. - GPU wait times can exceed 18 months, while rising HBM and DDR5 prices are pushing up system costs. - Dell overtook HPE for the top server market share, with 23.8% compared with HPE’s 20.9%. - Hyperion estimates the quantum computing market reached $1.4 billion in 2025, while 54% of respondents see a chance of a quantum winter. It has been, and will very likely continue to be, the “Roaring 2020's” for the HPC-AI data center industry. But similar to the generally healthy U.S. economy, affordability is a problem. Driven by demand for advanced computing technology, the HPC-AI data center infrastructure industry is generating tremendous growth, according to the latest market update figures released by industry analyst firm Hyperion Research. But with high demand come strains on supply chains that result in higher costs that restrain even higher growth. This is the picture presented this week by Hyperion at their annual breakfast at the SC26 Supercomputing Conference in Chicago. The customary large crowd turned out to hear Hyperion CEO Earl Joseph and colleagues discuss the state of the industry, some sectors of which are expanding at a clip Joseph said has never before been seen. “2025 was an extremely high growth year for the market…,” said Hyperion CEO Earl Joseph of on-premises servers for HPC, AI and data centers. “The first half of this year is growing at 20 percent… This is more than a doubling of historic growth. And then looking at the overall market in addition to servers, the storage, middleware, application services and spending for running HPC and AI for science workloads in the cloud…the market has just grown tremendously.” Among Hyperion’s key findings: - Overall HPC spending grew by just under 17 percent in 2025 reaching a total of more than $70 billion, including nearly 30 percent growth in cloud usage. - Worldwide sales of on-prem for HPC and AI-for-science servers reached $29.4 billion, an increase of nearly 15 percent, with the EMEA region growing by roughly 10 percent. - For the combination of HPC and AI-for-science on-prem servers plus cloud, the overall market is expected to double over the next five years, approaching $140 billion by 2030. - Growth in sales for on-prem servers during the first of this year was approximately 20 percent, and looking out to 2030, Hyperion projects sales to reach nearly $55 billion. Hyperion also disclosed that Dell has taken the top spot for servers from perennial leader HPE, with Dell capturing 23.8 percent market share versus HPE’s 20.9 percent share. HPC-AI Growth Runs Into Supply Chain Reality But these rosy growth figures generate pressure and unmet demands across the HPC-AI technology ecosystem, including processors, solid state drives (SSDs) and memory. For example, while more than 1 million GPUs were installed in 2025 – a roughly 25 percent growth rate over 2024 – there are reported wait times of 18 months or longer for new GPUs, which command higher prices. There also are the well-documented supply chain problems for memory. Hyperion Senior Vice President of Research Bob Sorensen said the rise in memory prices has added significantly to HPC systems pricing. A Hyperion study found that costs for high bandwidth memory (HBM) per gigabyte has increased since 2021 from between $9 and $11.50 to between $13 and $17 this year. Spread across the hundreds or thousands of nodes within a single system results in a powerful multiplier effect. Sorensen also cited prices for DDR5 SDRAM (Double Data Rate 5) synchronous dynamic random-access memory has jumped in price since 2021 by more than 300 percent. He compared pricing for an HPC system of around 600 petaflops ordered in 2023 compared to 2026 and found that system memory costs have increased from $35 million to more than $60 million, contributing to a complete system price of $125 million (up from $100 million four years ago) in which memory comprises 47 percent of total system cost. The AI boom means high demand and good times for memory vendors, but as Sorensen explained, memory is a volatile business. “Memory makers are loath to increase capacity,” he said. “They know the memory market is a boom bust sector…, they know that sooner or later demand is going to turn and they're going to be dealing with overcapacity or under capacity. So we don't see a real solution to this problem, at least for the next few years.” Cloud Adoption Accelerates as Quantum Computing Faces Uncertainty Hyperion also reported that cloud usage is increasing, with 80 percent of their survey respondents across industry, government and academia reporting utilizing cloud for some portion of their HPC and AI-for-science workloads. Hyperion Research Director Mark Nossokoff said industry sectors sites use cloud the most, according to Hyperion, compared with government organizations and academia. Leading factors favoring use of external clouds include the ability to dynamically add or remove resources, to access new hardware that is otherwise unavailable and to run jobs at scales not possible on-prem. Barriers to cloud adoption include concerns, “sometimes real, sometimes perceived,” Nossokoff said, that cloud is too expensive compared with on-prem. “There's also the difficulty in migrating existing applications to the cloud… We see that the government (sector) in particular identifies cost as being the highest issue and, interestingly, academia indicated that between costs and security, they didn't feel (cloud) met their requirements.” Sorensen also delivered an update on the quantum computing industry that included these highlights: - The global QC market in 2025 was estimated at $1.4 billion, wi

artigo.texto: A Netscout Systems, fornecedora de soluções de Observabilidade de rede, AIOps, Cibersegurança e proteção contra ataques DDoS, acaba de anunciar que sua estratégia de design sustentável proporciona aos usuários uma economia de 20% na eficiência energética dos produtos Netscout, diminuindo tanto os custos operacionais quanto o impacto ambiental. Esse resultado sustentável pode ser potencializado de acordo com a fonte de energia adotada. De acordo com uma pesquisa recente da BloombergNEF, a demanda global de eletricidade dos Data Centers quase quadruplicará até 2035, chegando a 2.354 terawatts-hora, o que representará 7% da demanda global de eletricidade. Materiais da Forrester destacam que a otimização de recursos se tornou responsabilidade de todos: “Os vencedores não vão debater ou se importar em rotular a resposta como ‘sustentabilidade’. Eles serão forçados a planejar IA, energia, água, terra, infraestrutura e impacto na comunidade de forma conjunta. Afinal, é isso que o crescimento resiliente exige atualmente.” Abordagem da Netscout na incorporação de sustentabilidade às suas soluções: Prioriza o design com eficiência de recursos tanto no nível dos componentes quanto da plataforma. Ajuda as organizações a mitigar os impactos ambientais e financeiros do rápido aumento no consumo de energia de Data Centers e IA. Permite a atualização de dispositivos mais antigos com um único equipamento (Appliance) para otimizar ainda mais a eficiência energética. Economia de Energia Comprovada Testes de desempenho em laboratório do equipamento InfiniStreamNG 3U compararam a plataforma M-series com a J-series. Os resultados mostraram redução no consumo de energia, gerando uma economia anual estimada de 1,3 MWh por dispositivo. Quando as perdas com refrigeração e distribuição de energia no Data Center são consideradas, a economia pode ser ainda maior. Resultados semelhantes foram observados em uma implantação real em ambiente de cliente. “A abordagem arquitetural de sustentabilidade desde a concepção da Netscout significa que priorizamos a eficiência energética no nível da plataforma e dos componentes”, disse Jillian James, diretora de sustentabilidade da Netscout. “Nós nos preocupamos com o impacto energético e de IA na Cadeia de uso de nossos clientes – e não apenas com as nossas próprias pegadas. Nosso objetivo é ajudar os clientes a tornar suas redes e análises melhores para o meio ambiente e mais eficientes no que diz respeito à preservação recursos.” Compromisso com a Sustentabilidade A plataforma M-series, com alta eficiência energética, reflete o compromisso corporativo mais amplo da Netscout com a responsabilidade ambiental. A Netscout está integrando ativamente a sustentabilidade em suas operações e ciclos de desenvolvimento de produtos para apoiar os princípios da economia circular. O menor consumo de energia proporcionado por esses produtos contribui para que a empresa avance em sua meta de reduzir a emissão de gases relacionados ao efeito estufa até 2030. Incorporando a eficiência energética ao design dos produtos, a Netscout ajuda os clientes a transformar a modernização da infraestrutura em valor duradouro para os negócios: custos operacionais mais baixos, menor impacto ambiental e maior capacidade para suportar as crescentes demandas digitais e de IA. A Plataforma M-series demonstra como o desempenho operacional e a sustentabilidade podem avançar juntos, ajudando as organizações a fazer um uso mais eficaz de energia, espaço e investimentos em infraestrutura. artigo.texto: Power Beast and T-MAX Plus take center stage as FOX ESS expands its commercial and industrial storage line-up AMSTERDAM, Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FOX ESS, a global leader in solar inverters and energy storage solutions, today hosted its flagship "UNLEASH THE BEAST" product launch event in Amsterdam. In front of over 200 industry partners and energy professionals, the company put two commercial and industrial (C&I) solutions at the center of the stage: Power Beast, which pairs the P3 Plus inverter series with the CQ7 and CQ20 battery systems, and T-MAX Plus, a liquid-cooled energy storage system built for large-scale applications. FOX ESS also unveiled the Fox Avocado S28 Plug-in Energy Storage System (ESS) for homes, further strengthening its portfolio across residential and C&I applications. The Beast Unleashed: Power Beast (P3 Plus inverter + CQ7/CQ batteries) Power Beast is the system behind the "Unleash the Beast" name. It pairs the P3 Plus split-type C&I inverter with a choice of two battery systems, the stackable CQ7 or CQ20 batteries. Installers get one platform that grows with the site, from a small commercial building to a large industrial installation. A single Power Beast system covers capacities from 28 kWh to 960 kWh and switches between on-grid and off-grid modes in 0 ms. Up to 100 units can be connected in parallel on-grid, and up to 30 units off-grid. P3 Plus Series: A range of split-type C&I inverters with power outputs from 50 kW to 125 kW. Featuring an IP65-rated die-cast enclosure, up to 200% PV input, eight MPPTs and three battery connection ports, the series offers flexibility in system design and battery integration. It supports integration with the CQ7 and CQ20 battery systems. CQ7 Battery Module: Each module offers 6.96 kWh of capacity and features an integrated battery heating system. Up to fourteen modules can be stacked vertically in one system. Thermal barriers between battery cells and module-level safety protection provide additional safety. CQ20 Battery System: Designed for indoor and outdoor applications, the CQ20 features an IP65-rated enclosure. Its integrated design combines the HV BOX and base to simplify installation, while built-in fire protection provides an additional layer of safety. System capacities range from 78.4 kWh to 958.08 kWh. Advancing C&I Energy Storage with T-MAX Plus A key highlight was the T-MAX Plus liquid-cooled C&I energy storage system, featuring 314Ah battery cells and integrated BMS, EMS, SMS, TMS and PCS for coordinated energy management and system protection. Supporting the parallel connection of up to 100 units, the system delivers up to 12.5MW/72.3 MWh of on-grid capacity. Its grid-forming capabilities also support off-grid operation, offering flexibility for a wide range of C&I applications. FOX ESS also introduced the T-MAX Plus 125 kW three-phase hybrid inverter. Described as the industry's first 125 kW C&I hybrid inverter, it integrates a Static Transfer Switch (STS) to enable seamless 0 ms switching between on-grid and off-grid modes. Direct connection to PV arrays, diesel generators and the utility grid provides businesses with greater flexibility in managing multiple energy sources. Fox Avocado S28: Plug In. Power Your Home. FOX ESS unveiled the Fox Avocado S28 Plug-in ESS, bringing a more accessible approach to home energy storage. Its integrated design and plug-and-play functionality simplify installation, while compatibility with existing solar systems, intelligent energy management and flexible battery expansion help households make better use of renewable energy and dynamic electricity tariffs. The Fox Avocado S28 is expected to launch in Q1 2027, with further details to be announced closer to release. A Comprehensive Portfolio for Diverse Energy Storage Needs FOX ESS also highlighted several product series that strengthen its residential and C&I portfolio: P100E Series: A residential energy storage solution offering power outputs from 2.5kW to 10kW (Up to 30kW parallel system) and storage capacities from 10kWh to 40kWh(Up to 120kWh parallel system). Key features include an IP66-rated die-cast enclosure, up to 200% PV input, 0 ms UPS switching and 95% depth of discharge (DoD). PQ1 and PQ3 Series: Modular, stackable all-in-one hybrid energy storage systems available in single-phase and three-phase configurations. Their design combines a top-mounted inverter with stackable battery modules, including the TQ5000-P, for flexible installation and capacity expansion. Intelligent Energy Management Powered by FoxCloud 2.0 At the heart of the FOX ESS ecosystem is FoxCloud 2.0, an intelligent energy management platform connecting FOX ESS products and enabling smarter energy control. Its AI Mode forecasts weather conditions and adjusts system operation according to users' electricity consumption habits and dynamic electricity prices. By optimizing when energy is stored and used, it helps users maintain a reliable power supply while maximizing potential energy savings and financial returns. FoxCloud 2.0 also offers real-time energy-flow tracking at five-second intervals, Virtual Power Plant (VPP) integration, one-click system diagnostics and over-the-air (OTA) firmware updates. By combining advanced hardware with intelligent software, FOX ESS helps users monitor their systems, make better use of renewable energy and optimize energy consumption.

artigo.texto: Chinese battery giants turn to Korean materials firms in an attempt to bypass U.S. and EU straightjacket Chinese battery makers including CATL are partnering with Korean materials suppliers and Western automakers to expand abroad as U.S. and European Union rules seek to reduce reliance on China-made EV batteries. Chinese battery makers are increasingly forging partnerships with companies around the world as they seek to overcome efforts by major economies to reduce their dependence on Chinese-made batteries, namely by courting Korean battery materials suppliers and leveraging the brands of U.S. and European automakers to expand their reach. On Nov. 18, Posco Group recently signed a long-term contract to supply lithium — a key raw material for lithium-ion batteries — for EV batteries to China's CATL, the world's largest battery maker, from 2026 to 2028 and has begun deliveries. This marks the first time Posco has supplied lithium to a Chinese battery manufacturer. Korean electrolyte producer Enchem has agreed to supply 350,000 tons of electrolyte to CATL through 2030, while Solus Advanced Materials is supplying copper foil produced at its Hungarian plant to CATL's European factories. Korean cathode and anode materials manufacturers are also seeking to supply Chinese battery companies. China has expanded its battery production capacity since the 2010s, backed by its vast domestic market and government support. Six Chinese battery manufacturers, including CATL and BYD, accounted for 56.4 percent of the global EV battery market outside China from January to September this year, up 13.3 percentage points from 43.1 percent during the same period last year, according to market researcher SNE Research. China has also established a virtual monopoly over the technology and materials supply chains for relatively inexpensive lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries. But despite their dominance in battery manufacturing, Chinese companies are reaching beyond their established supply chains as the United States and Europe increasingly emphasize reducing their reliance on Chinese batteries. The United States has implemented Prohibited Foreign Entity (PFE) regulations, which exclude companies from countries of concern, including China, and businesses under their influence from eligibility for the Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit. The restrictions will be tightened in stages to reduce the share of PFE-linked components and materials throughout the battery supply chain, including battery raw materials. Bypassing via partnerships CATL has found a way around these barriers by licensing its technology to U.S. automaker Ford. On Nov. 18, Ford announced that it had begun mass-producing and shipping batteries at its Michigan plant last month using CATL's LFP manufacturing technology — a destination the likes of which many onlookers wager that Korean-made battery materials and raw materials are likely to be used at. In Europe, where the EV market is expanding rapidly, local battery production has become a key priority. The European Commission proposed the Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA) in March, which would require EVs to contain a certain minimum proportion of European Union-made batteries and components to qualify for subsidies and public procurement benefits. The proposed legislation would also impose conditions on companies from countries accounting for more than 40 percent of global production capacity — effectively targeting China — when investing at least 100 million euros ($110 million) in the EU. Such companies would be required to establish joint ventures with local businesses or transfer technology. The legislation is still undergoing the legislative process. CATL and Gotion have already been expanding their European production bases through joint ventures with automakers such as Stellantis and Volkswagen. Their efforts could accelerate if the IAA takes effect, and their partnerships with Korean battery materials companies that have already established operations in Europe are part of the same strategy. "If demand for non-Chinese suppliers increases in local markets, reaching out to non-Chinese companies that already have operations there is a rational strategy," an industry insider said. A win-lose for Korea The issue is that the trend poses a challenge for Korea's three major battery manufacturers, because LG Energy Solution, SK On and Samsung SDI have sought to capitalize on U.S. restrictions against Chinese competitors as an opportunity to rebound, but Chinese companies' strategies to circumvent those restrictions could undermine their prospects. The three Korean companies' combined share of the global electric vehicle battery market outside China fell from 38.2 percent to 26.5 percent in the January-to-September period compared with a year earlier. The energy storage system (ESS) market, which Korea's three battery manufacturers are targeting as a new growth engine, may also not be immune to the growing competition as Ford plans to begin supplying ESS manufactured using CATL technology at its Kentucky plant in 2027. One silver lining for Korean battery makers could be that security concerns could remain a significant obstacle for Chinese-made energy storage systems in North America. "Energy storage systems used in artificial intelligence data centers retain detailed records of electricity consumption," an industry source said. "Security concerns are the biggest reason behind efforts to push Chinese-made energy storage systems out of North America." BY SUK GYEONG-MIN [yoon.soyeon@joongang.co.kr]

artigo.texto: The Chinese automaker is expected to sign a letter of intent with the Minas Gerais government in January 2027. The incoming administration’s priority is to attract investment to process lithium from the Jequitinhonha Valley and expand the electric-vehicle supply chain. BYD is expected to formalize a letter of intent for investments in Minas Gerais in January 2027. A report published by Brasil Mineral on November 25, 2026, said the understanding was reached at a meeting between executives from the Chinese automaker and representatives of the incoming state government. In addition to the possibility of building a vehicle factory, the talks include industrial processing of lithium extracted in the state. - BHP to invest up to US$17.4 billion in doubling South Australia’s copper output to 650,000 tons annually by 2040 - Brazil’s Geological Survey projects R$10.1 billion in social returns for 2025, with R$14.47 in benefits for every real invested - Rare earths cost nearly 11 times more in the United States than in China, fueling competition for Brazilian mineral projects - Three Cities in Pará Receive R$123.5 Million in Mining Royalties, Nearly One-Third of ANM’s Distribution to Municipalities However, no final decision has been made on whether to proceed with the projects. Minas Gerais aims to process lithium from the Jequitinhonha Valley The meeting took place in São Paulo on November 24, with Governor-elect Cleitinho Azevedo and representatives of BYD Brazil in attendance. Executives present included Tyler Li, the company’s president in Brazil, and Alexandre Baldy, senior vice president. According to Governor-elect Luís Eduardo Falcão, setting up an automotive plant is a secondary consideration in the current talks. The priority, therefore, is to develop a lithium processing and beneficiation plant. The incoming administration also plans to attract investment in other activities: - Battery manufacturing; - Renewable power generation; - Production of fast-charging equipment; - Development of the electric mobility industry. With this proposal, the incoming government aims to increase Minas Gerais’s share of the industrial stages that follow mining. BYD holds mineral rights covering 852 hectares in Minas Gerais The Chinese automaker’s interest in Brazil’s mineral resources did not begin with the recent talks. In February 2025, Reuters reported that BYD had acquired mineral rights covering 852 hectares in Coronel Murta, in the Jequitinhonha Valley. The acquisition took place in late 2023 through its subsidiary, BYD Exploração Mineral do Brasil. At the time of the report, however, the company was still conducting geological research and had no operating revenue. Other international companies are also exploring the region’s mineral potential. In September 2026, a Canadian mining company identified 12 new rare earth exploration targets in Lithium Valley, with indications of elements that are strategic for various industrial sectors. However, holding mineral rights does not guarantee that an area will become a commercial mine. Lithium processing could increase the value of Brazilian production Lithium is an important raw material for rechargeable batteries used in electric vehicles and energy storage systems. However, mining is only one stage of this supply chain. After extraction, the material must undergo industrial processing to meet the chemical specifications required by battery manufacturers. China currently has a strong presence in these processing stages. As a result, establishing processing facilities in Brazil could increase the country’s role in producing battery materials. Other South American countries are also seeking to expand the industry. In Argentina, for example, Eramet is considering a US$350 million investment to increase the capacity of a lithium plant. In Minas Gerais, however, decisions on the technology, production capacity and investment still depend on negotiations with the Chinese manufacturer. Minas Gerais also competes for a R$1 billion electric vehicle factory Another area of negotiations involves a new BYD facility that would manufacture electric commercial vehicles. Minas Gerais, São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro are competing for the project, which has an estimated investment of R$1 billion and the potential to create about 2,000 jobs. The expected start of operations under discussion is between 2028 and 2029. Meanwhile, the automaker is expanding its industrial presence in Bahia. The company is also preparing to launch the BYD Dolphin GT, a flex-fuel hybrid model slated for production in Camaçari. Despite talks with Minas Gerais, the company has not yet announced where it will build its new commercial vehicle factory. In addition, the estimated R$1 billion investment is not related to the lithium processing project, which still has no publicly disclosed budget. Letter of intent expected to be signed in January 2027 The next stage of negotiations is expected to take place after January 6, 2027, the scheduled inauguration date for the governor-elect. In addition to signing the document, the transition team is preparing a mission to China to learn about the electric mobility supply chain and discuss potential partnerships. For now, however, the letter of intent represents only a preliminary step in the negotiations. BYD has not yet confirmed the municipality that would host the lithium plant, the investment amount, its production capacity or the expected number of jobs. Should Brazil prioritize domestic lithium industrialization to increase its share of the global battery market? Sources: Brasil Mineral, published November 25, 2026; Diário do Comércio, published November 24, 2026; and Reuters, published February 14, 2025.

artigo.texto: Influential Women: Elizabeth 'Bess' Wildman, Builds People-First Leadership in Academic Healthcare Administration IL, UNITED STATES, November 23, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ -- Vice Dean for Academic Administration and Finance in the Biological Sciences Division at the University of Chicago, She Pairs Financial Discipline With a Lifelong Commitment to Developing Leaders Elizabeth âBessâ Wildman is a seasoned academic healthcare administrator and financial leader who serves as Vice Dean for Academic Administration and Finance in the Biological Sciences Division at the University of Chicago. With more than three decades of experience in healthcare administration, she oversees a broad portfolio spanning finance, human resources, information technology, clinical operations, and grants administration. Her work helps advance the institutionâs missions of patient care, education, and research. Bess brings strategic and financial discipline to complex academic medical operations, along with a strong commitment to authenticity, collaboration, and organizational development. Bess began her career in banking operations before moving into healthcare after earning her MBA from the Wake Forest University School of Business. She also holds a BA from the University of Virginia. Since entering the field, she has held leadership positions at multiple academic medical centers. Along the way, she has built significant experience with faculty practice plans and complex healthcare operations. That combination of financial training and operational depth has shaped the steady, strategic approach she brings to her current role. Her early grounding in banking gave her a practical understanding of financial operations that continues to inform her leadership of a large and varied administrative portfolio. Bess attributes her success to people. She has always been committed to developing others, particularly administrative fellows, and to mentoring her teams so they grow into outstanding leaders. Investing in people, supporting their growth, and helping them reach their full potential has been central to everything she has achieved. She takes particular pride in watching members of her teams become confident, capable leaders in their own right. For Bess, the growth of the people around her is the clearest measure of her own achievement. Her advice to young women entering healthcare administration begins with a frank observation: being a woman leader often requires an additional level of balance. She encourages young women to remain authentic to who they are while recognizing and navigating the different ways society may view women. Bess urges them to challenge inequities without adopting a victim posture. Above all, she tells them to know their value and to refuse to be walked over or overlooked. Bess sees healthcare in a significant period of disruption. Policy changes, the rapid growth of artificial intelligence, public intolerance of rising healthcare costs, and workforce shortages are all reshaping the landscape. At the same time, she views these pressures as a source of important opportunity. Precision medicine, in-home care, AI-enabled healthcare delivery, alternative providers, and new approaches to system-wide learning and workforce development all have the potential to transform the field. People-first leadership stands at the center of her values. Bess places a strong emphasis on developing talent, mentoring others, and helping people become outstanding leaders. Outside of work, family and active engagement in her community matter just as much to her. Together, these priorities guide how she leads, how she supports those around her, and how she contributes to the communities she serves. Her community involvement includes the University of Chicagoâs South Side community engagement efforts. Bess is also actively engaged with professional and leadership organizations, including the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC), the American College of Healthcare Executives (ACHE), Women of Impact, and CHIEF. These affiliations keep her connected to peers across academic medicine. She has also contributed to leadership networks focused on advancing women in healthcare. Across more than three decades, Bess has shown that sound financial stewardship and genuine investment in people can advance together. Her legacy is measured not only in the operations she oversees but in the leaders she has helped develop. For Elizabeth âBessâ Wildman, the lasting meaning of her work lies in a stronger, more equitable healthcare workforce prepared to meet a changing future.
