artigo.texto: O mercado de créditos de carbono ganhou espaço nas discussões da COP31, com avanços nas regras para comercialização internacional e na estruturação de mecanismos de financiamento voltados à preservação ambiental. Embora as negociações sobre combustíveis fósseis tenham enfrentado impasses e impedido um acordo final mais abrangente, a aprovação do artigo 6 representou um dos principais resultados da conferência nesse campo. O mecanismo permite que a conservação de florestas e a adoção de práticas produtivas sustentáveis também tenham valor econômico. Cada tonelada de dióxido de carbono (CO₂) retirada da atmosfera ou cuja emissão é evitada, por meio da manutenção da vegetação nativa e de sistemas como a agrofloresta cabruca, pode dar origem a um crédito de carbono, negociado para compensar emissões. O cenário entre a COP30 e a COP31 aponta mudanças importantes na governança climática e na destinação de recursos para projetos ambientais. Entre os avanços está a aprovação do comércio internacional de créditos de carbono com base no artigo 6, enquanto outros temas da agenda climática permaneceram sob impasse, especialmente aqueles relacionados aos combustíveis fósseis e à resistência de grandes países produtores. Outro destaque é o desenvolvimento do mercado regulado de carbono no Brasil. De acordo com a Secretaria Extraordinária de Mercado de Carbono, vinculada ao Ministério da Fazenda, o intervalo entre as duas conferências foi marcado pelo avanço na implementação desse sistema e pela consolidação de uma coalizão global voltada à cooperação internacional. Na área de financiamento, o presidente do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES), Aloizio Mercadante, mencionou a expectativa de captar aproximadamente 39 bilhões em investimentos destinados a iniciativas climáticas e projetos ambientais. Impactos para reservas ambientais e áreas de cabruca O fortalecimento dos instrumentos de financiamento climático também pode ampliar as oportunidades para proprietários de áreas protegidas, especialmente na Mata Atlântica. Nesse contexto, iniciativas de Pagamento por Serviços Ambientais (PSA) e ações de gestão territorial ganham relevância. A Reservas Votorantim, por exemplo, destaca benefícios associados à conservação de áreas de Mata Atlântica e Cerrado. Além da proteção contra invasões, desmatamentos e incêndios, os proprietários podem contar com suporte técnico e jurídico, isenções no Imposto sobre a Propriedade Territorial Rural (ITR) e participação em iniciativas como o PSA Carbonflor. Para acessar essas possibilidades, entretanto, é necessário que as áreas estejam organizadas do ponto de vista técnico e ambiental. Um exemplo é a Reserva Particular do Patrimônio Natural (RPPN) Serra dos Teiús, localizada em Ipiaú, no sul da Bahia. Reconhecida como unidade de conservação de interesse público e caráter perpétuo, a reserva possui 1,5649 hectare no bioma Mata Atlântica. Sua criação foi oficializada pela Portaria nº 007, de 29 de janeiro de 2026. Para propriedades com esse perfil, especialmente aquelas que desenvolvem ou têm potencial para sistemas agroflorestais de cabruca, a elaboração de um plano de manejo é uma etapa importante. O documento deve reunir informações sobre as condições ambientais da área, recursos hídricos, medidas de prevenção de ameaças, cronograma de atividades e indicadores de acompanhamento. Além de orientar a administração permanente da reserva, esse planejamento pode facilitar o acesso a programas de conservação e a iniciativas de financiamento climático.

artigo.texto: Global oil markets are heading… A TVA construction permit and… Data center proliferation will drive demand for natural gas in the United States over the next two years, Goldman Sachs has forecast, estimating that some 52 GW of new data center capacity could be added to the grid in 2028 alone. “Year-to-date, data-center power capacity and demand have increased by nearly 30% in the US, contributing to more than one third of US total power demand growth,” the bank’s analysts wrote in a note this week, as cited by Reuters. “We expect growth acceleration in data centers to be driven not only by a higher volume of facilities, but by increasingly larger physical footprints and higher power density,” they said. This will drive stronger growth in demand for electricity and, by extension, for natural gas, which has become the preferred method for data center operators to source reliable, baseload electricity since nuclear takes too long to build. That data centers are massive energy demand sources is no news. Indeed, data centers are the primary reason for upbeat demand growth projections in the natural gas industry. U.S. gas-fired power generation capacity in development directly tied to data centers nearly doubled to 189 GW in the first half of the year, and chances are the momentum continued in the second half as well. Data center operators like natural gas. And natural gas producers like data centers. No wonder, then, that U.S. natural gas production is on track to close a second consecutive year with record-high natural gas output as producers respond to demand signs both at home and overseas. Soaring demand for powering data centers combined with rising liquefied natural gas exports amid expanding liquefaction capacity, as well as surging global demand for spot LNG cargoes in the absence of Qatar’s gas due to the Iran war, is pushing American natural gas production higher this year. artigo.texto: 247 – A empresa aeroespacial SpaceX, do bilionário Elon Musk, recebeu autorização da Comissão Federal de Comunicações dos Estados Unidos (FCC) para implantar uma constelação de até 1 milhão de satélites destinados ao funcionamento de centros de processamento de dados no espaço. A iniciativa busca ampliar a infraestrutura necessária ao desenvolvimento da inteligência artificial (IA), utilizando a energia solar disponível em órbita terrestre. Segundo a CNN Brasil, trata-se da primeira autorização desse tipo concedida pela agência reguladora estadunidense. O projeto, denominado Starmind, pretende transferir parte da capacidade de processamento computacional para o espaço, com equipamentos capazes de atender à crescente demanda por serviços de inteligência artificial utilizados na Terra. A decisão representa um avanço nos planos da companhia de Musk de desenvolver centros de dados orbitais. A SpaceX defende que a instalação dessas estruturas fora do planeta permitirá aproveitar a energia solar e reduzir a pressão sobre recursos terrestres, especialmente água e eletricidade, empregados no funcionamento dos centros convencionais. Embora os equipamentos sejam instalados em órbita, sua finalidade será processar grandes volumes de informações destinados a aplicações terrestres. A proposta prevê a utilização de satélites como parte de uma infraestrutura computacional voltada ao atendimento das necessidades de processamento de sistemas avançados de IA. Governo dos EUA aposta em infraestrutura espacial para inteligência artificial A FCC apresentou a autorização como uma medida destinada a fortalecer a posição dos Estados Unidos no desenvolvimento de tecnologias avançadas. O órgão relacionou a expansão da infraestrutura computacional ao conceito de “superinteligência”, expressão utilizada pelo presidente Donald Trump para se referir à inteligência artificial. O presidente da comissão, Brendan Carr, afirmou que os Estados Unidos “lideram o mundo na era da superinteligência” e destacou a importância dos centros de processamento de dados para sustentar o avanço dessa tecnologia. “Essa ação abre fronteiras ousadas para a infraestrutura de computação necessária para impulsionar a liderança e o crescimento da América”, declarou Carr em comunicado divulgado pela agência. De acordo com a FCC, a autorização permitirá à SpaceX estabelecer a constelação Starmind com até 1 milhão de satélites de centros de dados, com o objetivo de “ajudar a atender à demanda em rápido crescimento por computação de superinteligência”. A dimensão do projeto coloca a infraestrutura espacial no centro da estratégia americana de expansão da capacidade computacional. A proposta da SpaceX é utilizar uma rede de equipamentos em órbita para realizar operações de processamento que atendam às necessidades de sistemas de inteligência artificial no planeta. SpaceX promete reduzir consumo de água e eletricidade na Terra Um dos principais argumentos apresentados pela companhia para justificar a instalação dos centros de dados no espaço é a possibilidade de aproveitar recursos energéticos disponíveis fora da superfície terrestre. A empresa sustenta que a utilização de energia solar em órbita poderá diminuir a necessidade de recursos empregados por instalações convencionais. Entre os benefícios anunciados estão a economia de eletricidade e a redução do consumo de água, recurso utilizado em sistemas de resfriamento de centros de processamento de dados. A iniciativa também pretende aproveitar o espaço disponível em órbita para ampliar a capacidade computacional. Os satélites funcionariam como unidades de processamento de informações, integradas a uma estrutura destinada a fornecer serviços para aplicações terrestres. Esses benefícios, entretanto, são apresentados como objetivos do projeto e não incluem resultados operacionais que permitam quantificar a economia de recursos ou demonstrar a eficiência da infraestrutura proposta. FCC relaciona projeto à civilização Kardashev tipo II Além dos argumentos econômicos e tecnológicos, a agência reguladora americana associou a autorização à possibilidade de avanço da humanidade em direção a uma civilização Kardashev tipo II. O conceito faz parte de uma classificação hipotética de civilizações segundo sua capacidade de aproveitar recursos energéticos. Nesse modelo, uma civilização do tipo II seria capaz de captar e utilizar a energia emitida por sua própria estrela, como o Sol. Ao mencionar essa classificação, a FCC vinculou o projeto da SpaceX a uma perspectiva de expansão do aproveitamento da energia solar para além da superfície terrestre. A referência, contudo, não significa que a implantação da constelação orbital permitiria alcançar esse estágio de desenvolvimento. Trata-se de uma associação feita pela agência entre a utilização de energia espacial e uma hipótese teórica sobre a evolução tecnológica das civilizações. Agência dos EUA poderá autorizar outros projetos A autorização concedida à SpaceX também abre um precedente regulatório para outras empresas interessadas em desenvolver infraestrutura de processamento de dados no espaço. Segundo a FCC, novos pedidos para o lançamento de satélites destinados a essa finalidade poderão ser analisados pela comissão. A decisão, portanto, não estabelece exclusividade para a companhia de Elon Musk nesse segmento. Embora o projeto Starmind tenha recebido autorização para uma constelação de até 1 milhão de equipamentos, as informações divulgadas não apresentam um cronograma detalhado para a implantação integral da rede.

artigo.texto: Base Power, a US-based energy company, has agreed with Cumberland Electric Membership Corporation (Cumberland EMC) to deploy 30 MW of residential battery storage in Tennessee. The batteries are to be installed across the service territory of the cooperative, where they will be linked as a networked fleet. Base is to install and maintain every unit, while Cumberland EMC will decide when the fleet charges and discharges. The cooperative will dispatch that fleet at system peaks in order to reduce demand and to cut its wholesale power costs. For its members, each battery is offered at $695 upfront plus $19 a month, and it can back up a home for up to 36 hours. The program is the first partnership that Base has formed in Tennessee and in the territory of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA). Installations are expected to begin in early 2027, and members can join a waitlist in the meantime. artigo.texto: Green Energy Storage (GES), an Italy-based maker of flow batteries for stationary storage, has received €10 million (~ $10.92 million) in financing from Intesa Sanpaolo. The bank has arranged it as a structured finance transaction through its Banca dei Territori division, which has worked with its IMI Corporate & Investment Banking division. The funds are to pay for the staff, materials and facilities that GES needs in order to scale up its hydrogen-manganese battery under the IPCEI programme. They are also to let the company run its first large-scale installations under real operating conditions, before the product is certified and industrialised. According to GES, the battery works at room temperature, and its power and energy modules can be sized independently of each other. The company, which is based in Povo in the province of Trento, has set itself the aim of reaching technology readiness level (TRL) 6 by the end of 2026. artigo.texto: A Odata Brasil recebeu autorização do Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade) para comprar uma empresa responsável pelo projeto de implantação do Data Center Anhanguera, localizado em Osasco, São Paulo. O ativo é atualmente controlado pela GP Participações Empresariais e pela Tattva, do grupo BEP Energia. A operação ainda depende do aval de outros órgãos antitruste. Ao Cade, as companhias informaram que o data center ainda não entrou em operação e que ainda não possui capacidade instalada. Atualmente, o data center detém apenas o parecer de acesso emitido pelo Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS), documento necessário para a conexão do empreendimento à Rede Básica do Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN). Caso a aquisição seja concluída e o projeto entre em operação, a empresa desenvolverá as mesmas atividades já exercidas pela Odata Brasil. Em manifestação ao Cade, a Odata destacou que a operação representa uma oportunidade de negócio alinhada à sua estratégia de desenvolvimento e expansão no mercado de data centers no Brasil. No momento, a companhia é responsável por oferecer colocation a clientes do segmento atacadista, incluindo provedores de nuvem em modelo hyperscale, empresas dos setores financeiro, de telecomunicações e diversas outras áreas com atuação em múltiplos segmentos. No Brasil, a Odata possui data centers nos estados de São Paulo e Rio de Janeiro, além de unidades na Colômbia, Chile e México. Já os vendedores destacaram que a venda pode contribuir para o desenvolvimento de seus negócios.

artigo.texto: Hindustan Zinc Limited (BSE: 500188; NSE: HINDZINC), the world’s largest integrated zinc producer, and the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras) have unveiled an electric three-wheeler prototype fitted with an approximately 1 kWh zinc-air battery designed to function as a range extender. Unveiled at the recently held IIT Madras Energy Summit 2026, the prototype marks a key stage in the research collaboration between the two institutions to develop indigenous zinc-based energy storage technologies for emerging applications. The unveiling was attended by Guest of Honour Praveen Chakravarthy, Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha); Amarendu Prakash, CEO and Whole-time Director, Hindustan Zinc; Prof. Manu Santhanam, Dean (ICSR), IIT Madras; and Dr. Aravind Kumar Chandiran of the Department of Chemical Engineering, IIT Madras, who led the project, along with other stakeholders. The three-wheeler uses a dual-battery configuration in which the zinc-air battery supplies nearly 10% of the vehicle’s total energy requirements. The lithium-ion battery supports acceleration and peak power demands, while the zinc-air unit provides a steady supply of energy during operation. The demonstration highlights how zinc-based batteries could complement existing energy storage systems in electric mobility. Zinc-air batteries generate electricity using zinc and oxygen from the surrounding air. The technology uses a non-flammable, water-based electrolyte and an abundant, recyclable metal, offering potential advantages in safety, affordability and environmental sustainability. India’s zinc resources also provide an opportunity to develop domestic energy storage capabilities and support the country’s energy self-reliance. The collaboration, initiated in 2024, has progressed from laboratory research to a vehicle-level demonstration. Amarendu Prakash, CEO and Whole-time Director, Hindustan Zinc, said, “At Hindustan Zinc, we are constantly exploring opportunities to expand the applications of zinc and unlock greater value from this versatile metal. With zinc being abundantly available in India, there is an opportunity to explore indigenous energy storage solutions that can contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat. Our collaboration with IIT Madras reflects our commitment to translating scientific research into practical applications, creating new demand avenues for zinc and strengthening its role in the global clean energy transition.” Congratulating the research team, Prof V Kamakoti, Director, IIT Madras, said, “Energy is the major focus of discussion globally, be it artificial intelligence, agriculture all the way to advanced manufacturing. Ensuring generation, storage and distribution of energy from different sources, specifically the renewable ones is the most important topic for research, development and commercialization. Our collaboration with Hindustan Zinc is yet another important effort towards this goal.” For Hindustan Zinc, a Vedanta Group company, the project forms part of its wider effort to develop new applications for zinc and expand its value-added product portfolio. Under its HZL 2.0 growth and diversification strategy, the company is exploring zinc-based battery technologies for renewable energy storage and electric mobility. Hindustan Zinc Limited (BSE: 500188; NSE: HINDZINC), a Vedanta Group company, is the world’s largest integrated zinc producer and among the top 10 silver producers globally. The company supplies more than 30 countries and holds approximately 74% of India’s primary zinc market. It was recognised as the world’s most sustainable company in the metals and mining category for the third consecutive year in the S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment 2025 and became the first Indian company to join the International Council on Mining & Metals in 2025. Its initiatives include EcoZen, Asia’s first low-carbon green zinc brand, a 3.32-times water-positive certification and a Net Zero emissions target by 2050 or sooner. Its social welfare programmes reach 2.6 million people. Established in 1959, IIT Madras is an Institute of National Importance with 18 academic departments and several interdisciplinary research centres. It offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes across science and technology disciplines. Recognised as an Institution of Eminence in 2019, it ranked first in the Overall category for the seventh consecutive year and in the Engineering category for the tenth consecutive year in the NIRF India Rankings 2025.

artigo.texto: Pathways for reforming the New Zealand Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS) are available and feasible, but the window to act is closing and deferring policy change beyond 2030 could forgo $11 billion to $12 billion in auction revenue through to 2035, a group of researchers say. “Our concern is that within a few years, we’re going to reach a stage where the NZ ETS really doesn’t serve anyone’s interests. It’s not going to work for high emitters, for low emitters, for foresters, for iwi and Māori, for taxpayers, for future generations - and if it doesn’t work for them, then it doesn’t work for government,” Catherine Leining, policy fellow at economics organisation Motu Research, said in a webinar on Thursday morning. Alongside Leining, Motu Research analyst Ikerne Aguirre, Kapiti Climate director Kristen Green and Victoria University of Wellington associate professor Julia Talbot-Jones, produced a working paper called ‘Scoping NZ ETS and removals pathways for better climate and nature outcomes.’ Publicly released on Thursday, the researchers said through their working paper, they were interested in finding solutions that would work better than the status quo for everyone. Leining made clear that she and other researchers were not presenting an implementation plan, proposal or recommended pathway at this time. “We’re hoping that this work will lead to deeper research and to dialogue.” ETS ‘must evolve to deliver on NZ’s climate targets’ The ETS prices emissions by requiring certain sectors of the economy to have "surrender obligations" for the greenhouse gases they release into the atmosphere. These sectors include forestry, liquid fossil fuels, stationary energy, industrial processes, synthetic greenhouse gases, and waste. The ETS was initially set up to help NZ meet its 2050 net emissions target and international obligations under the Paris Agreement. Changes to climate change law removed a provision which stated the ETS unit volumes and price control regulations must "accord with" Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) under the Paris Agreement. In the working paper, the researchers said the ETS was based on outdated assumptions “and must evolve to deliver on New Zealand’s climate targets and send clear long-term investment signals to emitters and foresters." “By the mid-2030s, the Government will progressively lose control over unit supply and prices, placing market stability and climate targets at risk. The substitution of forestry removals for feasible emissions reductions is delaying decarbonisation and creating intergenerational risks.” Alongside this, the paper said "deferring policy change beyond 2030 could forgo around $11 billion to $12 billion in auction revenue through 2035". Calls for ETS reform are not new, with Parliamentary Commissioner for the Environment Simon Upton saying in August that it was a question of ‘when’ not ‘if’ reform happens. A Removals Investment Mechanism The researchers said a complementary Removals Investment Mechanism (RIM) alongside ETS reforms could improve outcomes. “Under current settings, a single price signal cannot deliver both the decarbonisation and removals New Zealand needs in the long term. A RIM would combine government- and market-driven incentives with policies and regulations to value removals for their climate and wider benefits, such as biodiversity and resilience. “A RIM could be used alongside any NZ ETS pathway to boost and diversify investment in forestry and other removals without displacing emissions reductions. This would help with meeting current climate targets - and more ambitious future targets in response to temperature overshoot.” Scenarios were modelled for alternative ETS pathways - this included how the status quo, a pathway with constrained removals in the ETS, and a pathway with no removals in the ETS could impact emissions prices, climate targets, afforestation and fiscal outcomes with and without a RIM. The paper said the RIM could operate independently from a NZ ETS, trading only in gross emissions or in conjunction with an ETS trading in both gross emissions and removals. The role of the RIM would increase with greater constraints on removals in the NZ ETS and the role of supporting policies would increase alongside greater reliance on "least-cost" forestry removals to achieve climate targets, the paper said. “Depending on design, a RIM could be used to help maintain government control over climate targets and NZ ETS market stability, send clearer investment signals for emitters and foresters, generate net revenue for the Crown, and improve outcomes for climate and nature.” “It could be designed in ways that maintain or increase the value of existing and new removals investments relative to the status quo NZ ETS. The RIM modelled in this paper is a hypothetical illustration for demonstrating proof of concept, not a proposal or recommendation, and additional approaches should be considered," the paper said. Policy development should start now, researchers say Leining said the window to act was closing and the policy development process needs to start now as it was slow and took time. “We need inclusive processes and well-signaled outcomes that maintain investment value and market confidence.” The working paper said to avoid market disruption, government decision-making on introducing a RIM would need to be staged carefully and be "shaped and informed by inclusive processes with full regards to the rights, interests, and aspirations of iwi and Māori; and concluded well in advance of implementation.” “Process guardrails would be essential to build confidence in policy change and ensure a just transition for NZ ETS participants, iwi and Māori, broader stakeholders, and communities.” Policy development should start now, the paper said. “Given the lead time required, the process of policy development should begin as soon as possible, while the Government still holds the lever of auctioning and before misdirected investme

artigo.texto: Oman BESS Projects are moving through the procurement stage, with bidders receiving additional time to prepare proposals for five standalone battery energy storage facilities. The programme will deliver 950MW of combined power capacity and 3,800MWh of energy storage across five locations. Nama Power & Water Procurement Company (Nama PWP) is overseeing the independent power producer (IPP) tender. The deadline extension gives prospective developers more time to complete their technical and commercial submissions. Meanwhile, the procurement represents a significant investment in Oman’s electricity infrastructure. It will strengthen grid flexibility and support the country’s expanding renewable energy generation capacity. MEED reported the latest bidding extension on November 23, 2026. However, the revised submission deadline and total construction cost have not been publicly confirmed. Oman BESS Projects cover five construction locations The procurement comprises five standalone battery energy storage system (BESS) facilities distributed across four governorates. Together, the installations will provide 950MW of power capacity and 3,800MWh of storage. The largest installation will occupy approximately 149,535 square metres in Sohar, Al Batinah North Governorate. It will deliver 500MW of power capacity and 2,000MWh of storage. Furthermore, the facility will connect to Oman’s electricity grid through a 220kV connection. Four additional installations will provide the remaining 450MW of capacity. The Al Mabellah facility in Muscat Governorate will deliver 100MW and 400MWh of storage. It will connect to the electricity network through a 132kV connection. Similarly, the Ayjah facility in South Al Sharqiyah Governorate will provide 100MW and 400MWh. Its planned grid connection will also operate at 132kV. The Jalan Bani Bu Ali installation will contribute 150MW and 600MWh of storage. Its connection will involve the Sadah and Jalan Bani Bu Ali wind farm substations. Meanwhile, the Sadah facility in Dhofar Governorate will deliver 100MW and 400MWh. It will connect to the Sadah wind farm substations through a 132kV connection. The five installations will collectively provide four hours of storage at their combined rated power capacity. Consequently, they will help balance electricity supply and demand during periods of fluctuating generation. Separately, Oman is advancing a 1GW battery storage development under a $1 billion agreement between Nama Holding and China’s State Grid International Development. The programme covers two 500MW installations at Duqm Industrial Station and Al-Subaikhi Station in Ibri. The Duqm-Ibri BESS project is distinct from Nama PWP’s 950MW procurement, although both initiatives will strengthen grid flexibility and support renewable energy integration. Oman BESS Projects support renewable energy integration The procurement aligns with Oman’s strategy to increase renewable energy generation and strengthen electricity supply security. Nama PWP’s 2026–2032 Power Seven-Year Statement identifies energy storage as an important component of future electricity planning. The company highlights battery storage’s potential to support renewable integration and peak-demand management. According to the statement, renewable sources contributed approximately 9% of Oman’s electricity production in 2025. The country targets increasing this contribution to at least 30% by 2030. Consequently, large-scale storage infrastructure will become increasingly important as additional solar and wind projects enter development. Battery systems can store surplus electricity and release it when renewable generation declines. Meanwhile, Oman’s electricity demand continues to increase. Nama PWP projects peak demand across the Main Interconnected System will rise from 7,863MW in 2025 to 14,147MW by 2032. The five facilities will therefore strengthen the electricity system’s flexibility and capacity management. They will also complement investments in renewable generation and transmission infrastructure. The procurement also comes alongside a separate 1GW battery storage agreement involving Nama Holding and China’s State Grid International Development. Signed in November 2026, that agreement covers two 500MW facilities at Duqm Industrial Station and Al Subaikhi Station. The Oman Investment Authority valued those separate developments at approximately US$1 billion. However, the agreement does not represent the financial value of the five-facility procurement managed by Nama PWP. The five-facility procurement remains at the competitive bidding stage. Nama PWP will proceed with the developer selection process following the submission of proposals. The successful developers will subsequently advance the facilities towards financing, construction and eventual operation.

artigo.texto: Botetourt County says Google data center construction could wind down over next week BOTETOURT COUNTY, Va. (WSET) — Construction activity at Google's proposed data center in Botetourt County could continue for several more days, even after a judge voided the county's agreement with the company. Botetourt County Communications Coordinator Brent Watts says the county learned from its board chair that activity at the site could continue for the next several days, possibly another week. Watts says crews need time to wind down construction and secure equipment already at the site. "They have to wind down construction. They can't just pack up and leave because there's a lot of things that are there that have to be kind of buttoned up," Watts said. The update comes as nearby residents continue looking for answers about what the court ruling means for the project. RELATED: Judge rules Botetourt County Google data center deal violated law, halts construction Courtney Pritt lives about 1,500 feet from the proposed data center site. She says her family thought they had found their forever home, but the project has already brought concerns about noise. "The first time we heard the blasting, I ran outside to get the dogs, who just froze in place, and I took them inside. That was not a great experience," Pritt said. Even after the judge's ruling, Pritt says she noticed activity at the property, including pallets being brought onto the site. She contacted the sheriff's office for answers but says she was directed elsewhere. "I'm just wondering who will be enforcing this?" she asked. Her son, Cooper Pritt, has seen data centers firsthand while training in Leesville. He worries about what the development could mean for the surrounding landscape. "They honestly look like prisons. They're gated- barbed wire fences, just really dark. I feel like this here is a really bright land, and it's just going to drain everything out of it. All of the color, all of the life," Cooper said. ABC13 went to the construction site to ask workers whether construction was still underway. They declined to comment. We also took questions directly to members of the Board of Supervisors. Board member Brandon Nicely said the county is still weighing its options following the judge's decision. "What will you do to make sure you're more transparent with people from now on?" ABC 13 asked. "Well, it's up to our attorneys and all that to make sure we don't get out of line. We felt like we were, so, you know, we acted what we thought was perfectly legal. I think we still have a little bit of... We don't really care for the judgment that much, as anybody would, but we're trying to decide which way we want to go now, so we're going to do our best," Nicely said. But several major questions remain unanswered. ABC13 asked county leaders what will happen to Google's money that has already been spent on capital improvements, whether the county plans to appeal the ruling and what Google's next steps will be. We also asked whether the county plans to hold another vote on the agreement. Board members declined to comment on those questions. For families like the Pritts, the uncertainty continues as they wait to learn what will happen next with the project just down the road from their home. ABC13 will continue following the county's response and Google's next steps.

artigo.texto: JASPER – Artificial Intelligence data centers are cropping up around the nation, bringing many questions from residents who live in highly sought after locations for their construction. Citizen Action Coalition (CAC) hosted an informative program to educate the public with a forum titled “How Data Centers Impact Communities,” held Monday, November 9, at the Astra Theater in Jasper. Projects are rumored in the southwest region, said host Bryce Gustafson, program organizer with CAC, to an ample crowd gathered at the theater. “They're trying to put these things in the pathway of least resistance,” he said. “We’re known as the Crossroads of America,” Gustafson continued, explaining Indiana has a lot of national infrastructure crisscrossing Indiana, such as interstate highways, electric lines, natural gas lines, fibre optics and complimented by cheap land. “Low cost of labor and our taxes are low,” he added. “Pretty much everywhere [in Indiana] is close to a large population,” Gustafson continued, noting Indianapolis, Detroit, Chicago, Columbus and others. “For the most part, we don’t have a lot of natural disaster risks,” he said. Indiana is at low risk for hurricanes and wildfires. Addressing the impacts of AI data Centers to communities and infrastructure, Gustafson started with the lack of transparency and accountability. “This has happened in many places across the state,” he said, “when you have elected officials signing NDAs [non disclosure agreements] … having meetings behind closed doors, when all of a sudden, we have a data center coming.” Gustafson used the town of Monrovia in Indiana, where about 550 acres of farmland and woods were rezoned and plans were revealed for six buildings and a substation, according to the Indiana Daily Student out of Bloomington, Indiana. At the forum Gustafson revealed the project was a Google AI data center. “The developer turned out to be Google,” he said. “They had their lawyer do a town hall one week. Two weeks later it was in front of the planning commission. A week after that, it was in front of the commissioners and they passed it through,” he said. “The public had three weeks to understand what was going on.” “If you’re so keen on these data centers, these projects, you have to have community community buy-in,” Gustafson said. According to wfwyi.org, CAC has publicly raised concerns about confidential information associated with the Monrovia project. Energy and water consumption for one data center project uses a little less than 10% of what the state uses, Gustafson said. “Water consumption is a big thing,” he continued. He explained about a data center project in 2023 in New Carlisle, Indiana, where the county commissioners said the project could take up to 24 millions gallons of water out of the aquifer. The industry response, he said, was “Don’t worry about it, we’re going to do a closed [water] system,” though Gustafson said no one from the industry explained the system. Moving on to air pollution, Gustafson said data centers had backup power generators, which were typically diesel powered generators. “If the power grid goes down, they will have to fire those things up,” he said, explaining that generators produce greater noise and pollution than the data center does on a daily basis. Data center noise can reach 65 decibels, he said. According to the Environmental Resilience Institute at Indiana University, “External noise levels can range from 55 to 85 A-weighted decibels (dBA) … comparable to a busy street. “Noise levels exceeding 85 dBA are harmful to hearing, creating a risk for surrounding communities and wildlife,” as read in the article, “Data centers: An overview for Hoosier communities,” found at https://eri.iu.edu/resources/fact-sheets/data-centers.html. Memory chips are in high demand due to data centers. Chips are used in common digital devices, such as phones and personal computers. The demand for chips have made them hard to get, Gustafson explained, which drives up the costs of our consumer products. “We have chips in our phones and computers, and those costs are being shouldered by us,” he said. Data centers create a “heat island effect,” he said. “You have servers that are running very hot and that heat is going to dissipate into the community around it.” Gustafson said Indiana utilities as a whole are spending tens of millions of dollars on infrastructure to service data centers. The industry, he said is looking to use gas powered energy plants to power data centers. Small modular reactors, or nuclear power, is being considered but no such facilities are operating in the United States. Indiana Senate Enrollment Act 425 was signed into law May 6, 2025, which defines an energy production zone. According to IN Code 8-1-8.2-2, an "energy production zone" means a premise of land on which any of the following was located as of January 1, 2025: “An electric generation facility with a generating capacity of at least eighty (80) megawatts, regardless of whether the electric generation facility is operational; A surface or underground mine at which mining operations are no longer occurring. “The term does not include a premise of land on which either of the following was located as of January 1, 2025: “One (1) or more wind power devices (as defined in IC 8-1-41-7 ) that are integrated into an electric generation facility; One (1) or more commercial solar energy systems (as defined in IC 8-1-42-2 ),” according to https://law.justia.com/codes/indiana/title-8/article-1/chapter-8-2/section-8-1-8-2-2/. Gustafson stated, “If you’re on energy production zones, then the locals have no say.” He noted Spencer County has energy production zones. artigo.texto: Larsen & Toubro (L&T), through two of its verticals, namely its Renewables business and L&T Electronic Products & Systems (LTEPS), has jointly secured a 300 MW/900 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) order. According to an L&T press release, the order is for a BESS project at Khavda in Gujarat, with a three-hour storage duration. The project will have a power capacity of 300 MW and an energy storage capacity of 900 MWh. By storing surplus renewable energy during periods of high generation and releasing it during peak demand, the system will help maximise clean energy utilisation, strengthen grid stability, and enhance the flexibility and reliability of power supply. L&T Uses Liquid-Cooling Technology The advanced BESS solution will incorporate liquid-cooling technology to deliver higher power density, enhanced safety, and a longer operating life. The facility will play a crucial role in improving grid flexibility and enabling greater integration of renewable energy into India's power network. The order further strengthens L&T's position in the energy storage sector and reflects the trust and confidence that clients place in the Company's ability to deliver complex projects at scale. Building L&T's BESS Business Since Larsen & Toubro (L&T) carved out a separate renewable energy vertical within its infrastructure segment in 2024, the company has seen rapid growth in its renewable energy and energy storage businesses. L&T recently secured orders for three Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) projects from a Middle Eastern client, collectively contributing 6 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of storage capacity. The projects feature four-hour BESS installations, each capable of storing and dispatching energy to support grid stability and renewable energy integration.

https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBM.resumo: A expansão da infraestrutura de data centers no Brasil entrou no centro de uma nova disputa sobre incentivos fiscais, financiamento público e soberania digital. A Coalizão Direitos na Rede (CDR) critica o Projeto de Lei 305/2026, que institui o Programa de Desenvolvimento de Data Centers Regionais (PRODATA BRASIL), por prever benefícios a grandes empreendimentos sem estabelecer garantias suficientes de proteção ambiental, participação das comunidades e desenvolvimento tecnológico nacional. De autoria do deputado federal Duda Ramos (PODE/RR), o projeto prevê incentivos tributários para a instalação de data centers nas regiões Norte e Nordeste, prioridade no acesso a financiamentos do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) e da Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (Finep), além de garantias ao capital estrangeiro. Para a CDR, a proposta repete problemas identificados na mobilização contra o REDATA (PL 278/2026), que também previa incentivos fiscais para o setor sem estabelecer previamente salvaguardas socioambientais e mecanismos para assegurar a soberania digital brasileira. A entidade não se opõe à expansão da infraestrutura digital, mas questiona o modelo de atração de investimentos baseado em benefícios ao setor privado sem contrapartidas que garantam retorno econômico, tecnológico e social ao país. "Não somos contra o desenvolvimento tecnológico nem contra investimentos em infraestrutura digital. Somos contra um modelo que oferece benefícios ao setor privado antes de garantir direitos, proteger os territórios e assegurar que a riqueza e o conhecimento gerados permaneçam no Brasil", afirma André Fernandes, fundador e integrante da diretoria do IP.rec (Instituto de Pesquisa em Direito e Tecnologia do Recife), entidade integrante da CDR. Demanda por energia e água entra no debate Um dos principais pontos de preocupação envolve o impacto ambiental dos empreendimentos. Data centers demandam grandes volumes de energia e água e ocupam extensas áreas territoriais. Na avaliação da Coalizão, a disputa entre estados para atrair esses investimentos pode resultar em renúncias fiscais, oferta de terrenos, infraestrutura dedicada, prioridade de acesso à rede elétrica e flexibilização de exigências. A entidade também questiona a capacidade de geração de benefícios econômicos de longo prazo. A instalação física de servidores, argumenta a CDR, não assegura a criação de empregos duradouros, o desenvolvimento de tecnologia nacional, a realização de pesquisas científicas ou a formação de um ecossistema local de inovação. O projeto prevê diretrizes de sustentabilidade, como utilização de fontes renováveis, redução do consumo de água e gestão de resíduos. Para a Coalizão, entretanto, essas medidas não substituem avaliações de impactos cumulativos, licenciamento ambiental adequado e participação efetiva das comunidades afetadas, incluindo consulta prévia, livre e informada aos povos indígenas, quando aplicável. Outro questionamento diz respeito à ausência de critérios detalhados para enquadramento dos empreendimentos, monitoramento, transparência e avaliação dos resultados. Esses aspectos, segundo a entidade, ficam para regulamentação posterior. A CDR cobra do Congresso Nacional a realização de um debate público e a definição de contrapartidas concretas antes do avanço do PL 305/2026. Para a organização, a política de expansão dos data centers precisa considerar não apenas a capacidade de atrair infraestrutura e capital estrangeiro, mas também o controle dos recursos estratégicos, a proteção dos territórios e a geração de conhecimento e tecnologia no Brasil.

artigo.texto: Por que os data centers de IA fazem tanto barulho? Veja vídeo Qual o som da inteligência artificial? Ou melhor, o som de um centro de dados de IA? Esse é um dos motivos pelos quais praticamente ninguém quer ter um desses data centers como vizinho. Mas o Brasil já concentra quase metade de todos os data centers da América Latina, e até 2030 esse mercado deve dobrar de tamanho. Então, cada vez mais brasileiros terão um deles como vizinho. Mas voltando ao barulho, de onde ele vem? Os centros de dados abrigam milhares de computadores. E, assim como o seu laptop, esses computadores esquentam quando estão trabalhando muito. Isso acontece porque, dentro dos computadores, existem pequenos chips que realizam incontáveis cálculos a cada segundo para manter a internet funcionando, transmitir vídeos e alimentar sistemas de IA. À medida que a eletricidade passa pelos chips, uma pequena parte dessa energia é convertida em calor a cada cálculo realizado. artigo.texto: Internacional EUA autorizam SpaceX a lançar até 1 milhão de satélites de data centers Projeto de Elon Musk prevê criar uma estrutura de processamento de dados em órbita para atender à demanda por inteligência artificial Foto: Imagem gerada com auxílio de IA A SpaceX recebeu autorização inédita nos Estados Unidos para instalar data centers no espaço. A decisão da Comissão Federal de Comunicações (FCC) permite que a empresa de Elon Musk lance uma constelação com até 1 milhão de satélites destinados ao processamento de dados. Batizado de Starmind, o projeto pretende ampliar a capacidade de computação necessária para atender à crescente demanda por inteligência artificial. Em comunicado, a FCC afirmou que a medida busca fortalecer a posição americana na chamada economia de superinteligência. O termo é utilizado pelo presidente Donald Trump para se referir à inteligência artificial. A proposta da companhia é aproveitar a energia solar e a disponibilidade de espaço em órbita para operar os equipamentos. Apesar de estarem fora da Terra, os satélites serão utilizados para processar grandes volumes de dados destinados a aplicações no planeta. Projeto prevê reduzir consumo de recursos na Terra A SpaceX defende que a instalação de data centers em órbita pode diminuir a pressão sobre recursos terrestres, como água e energia elétrica, utilizados na operação dessas estruturas. O presidente da FCC, Brendan Carr, afirmou que os Estados Unidos estão à frente na corrida pela superinteligência e destacou a importância dos centros de processamento para o desenvolvimento da tecnologia. "Essa ação abre fronteiras ousadas para a infraestrutura de computação necessária para impulsionar a liderança e o crescimento da América", afirmou. Em outro trecho do comunicado, a agência relacionou a iniciativa à possibilidade de os Estados Unidos avançarem em direção a uma civilização Kardashev tipo II. A classificação descreve uma civilização hipotética capaz de captar e utilizar a energia emitida por sua estrela, no caso da Terra, o Sol. A autorização concedida à SpaceX é a primeira desse tipo no país. artigo.texto: Often referred to as the data center capital of the world, Loudoun County has launched an informational dashboard with interactive maps and easy-to-use fact sheets to help inform residents and other localities about the industry’s footprint here. The initiative started from a request by Supervisor Koran T. Saines (D-Sterling) that the staff put together a data center fact sheet to help educate residents looking for more information. Public Affairs and Communications Officer Glen Barbour told supervisors the staff had prepared a fact sheet but that there was more information than what could fit on a single page, so they developed a larger platform. The webpage covers topics including the history of data centers in Loudoun, a dashboard with the industry’s square footage by election district, answers to questions about water, noise, air quality, tax revenue, public safety, energy considerations, electrical infrastructure, substations, back-up generators, on-site power generation, appearance, land values, workforce and land use. The page will also be a helpful for other jurisdictions looking for information, Barbour said. “This resource, this information about data centers in Loudoun is intended to help anyone begin their research on our website and find answers to commonly asked information. This resource has helped relieve a great burden on staff in Loudoun because we’re able to refer inquires to the website as a starting point. I know that many staff in planning and zoning have referred planners in other jurisdictions to the website and I also have referred countless news organization from around the world to loudoun.gov/datacenters,” Barbour said. The information required collaboration between the county’s departments of Planning and Zoning, Building and Development, General Services, Information Technology, Economic Development, Fire and Rescue, Health Department, Mapping and GIS, county attorney, Management and Budget and Public Information. “Development of the content required a whole-of-county approach because so many different departments hold various types of data related to this topic,” he said. Notably, the webpage includes an interactive map that shows every data center in Loudoun, and where it is in the process: built or under construction, approved, or in review. It allows residents to search for an address and see nearby data center sites and select those sites to see more information. That information includes the parcel pin, building permit issue date, year built and square footage. According to the most recent data on the dashboard, the county currently has 58.3 million square feet of data centers built or under construction, totaling 245 buildings. Another 33.8 million square feet are approved or under by-right review, totaling an additional 114 buildings. Another 21 million square feet are under legislative review, totaling 54 buildings. The Sterling election district is home to the largest concentration of data centers with 25 million square feet. Broad Run follows with 15 million. Algonkian and Catoctin are the county’s only two election districts without any data centers. The information included on the site was last updated Sept. 1, 2026. Learn more at loudoun.gov/datacenters.

artigo.texto: 24 horas com o VERDADEIRO PREMIUM da Motorola! PRIMEIRAS IMPRESSÕES do Motorola Signature 27! O TecMundo testou por um dia inteiro em primeira mão o novo Motorola Signature 27 no Rio de Janeiro!. Após diversos rumores e vazamentos, a Motorola enfim anunciou a chegada do Motorola Edge 70 Neo, seu novo smartphone intermediário da série 70. O modelo traz um conjunto de especificações até bem competente, como uma câmera primária de 50 megapixels e uma bateria de 7.000 mAh. O grande destaque desse lançamento da Motorola é justamente essa bateria mais parruda, que se tornou tendência entre os aparelhos intermediários de diversas fabricantes. Esse modelo ostenta os 7.000 mAh e oferece capacidade suficiente para pelo menos dois dias de uso contínuo, além da compatibilidade com carregamento de 45W. No quesito das câmeras, o conjunto também não decepciona e a companhia entrega uma ilha traseira com sensor primário de 50 MP por meio do sensor Sony LYTIA 710 (f/1.8). Ao lado desse componente, foi inserido um pequeno sensor macro de dois megapixels para fotografar objetos muito próximos. A câmera frontal tem 32 MP para as selfies. Tela, processador e disponibilidade As demais especificações do Motorola Edge 70 Neo ainda são interessantes, pois a companhia montou esse smartphone com uma tela bem grande de 6,8 polegadas. Esse display funciona por meio de um painel Extreme AMOLED na resolução de 2.772 x 1.272 pixels, com taxa de atualização de 144 Hz e brilho máximo de 5.200 nits. Já na parte mais interna, quem comanda todas as operações do celular é o Snapdragon 7s Gen 3, uma plataforma lançada pela Qualcomm em meados de 2024 para smartphones intermediários. Para completar o trio dessas especificações, há opções únicas de 8 GB de memória e 128 GB de armazenamento, expansível até 1 TB via cartão microSD. - O modelo da Motorola chega com Android 16 de fábrica e a companhia promete três anos de atualizações do sistema operacional e cinco anos de updates de segurança; - Há proteção Corning Gorilla Glass 7i no vidro e durabilidade militar MIL-STD-810H; - Ele será vendido nas cores Pantone Gray Lilac, Milky Blue, Mountain View e Sage. Por enquanto, o Motorola Edge 70 Neo estará disponível apenas na Índia por 34.999 rúpias indianas (cerca de R$ 2.200 em conversão direta). Ainda não há informações sobre o lançamento para outros países. Ficha técnica Já que o assunto é celular, a versão beta da One UI 9.5 trouxe novidades como o App Lock, Tap to Share e mais opções de personalização. artigo.texto: Novo sistema de comércio de emissões deve aumentar a demanda por créditos de carbono e atrair investidores para projetos ambientais FOTO: Magnific ECONOMIA VERDE Regulamentação do mercado de carbono pode ampliar investimentos no Brasil a partir de 2027 Por Redação A regulamentação do mercado de carbono no Brasil pode abrir uma nova frente de investimentos e ampliar a participação do país no setor de ativos ambientais. Com a criação do Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões (SBCE), instituído pela Lei nº 15.042/2024, o país avança na estruturação de um mercado regulado, que funcionará paralelamente às negociações voluntárias já existentes. O modelo prevê a inclusão gradual de 16 setores econômicos até 2031, quando o sistema deverá estar plenamente operacional. Empresas que ultrapassarem 25 mil toneladas anuais de emissões de dióxido de carbono equivalente estarão sujeitas a limites de emissão e poderão precisar adquirir cotas para compensar os volumes excedentes. Entre os segmentos previstos para as primeiras etapas estão alumínio, siderurgia, cimento, petróleo e gás natural, papel e celulose e vidro. A expectativa é que a regulamentação amplie a demanda por créditos ambientais e crie oportunidades para empresas, gestores de recursos e fundos de investimento. O sistema será baseado no mecanismo conhecido como cap and trade, pelo qual o governo estabelece limites de emissões e permite a negociação de cotas. Empresas que emitirem abaixo do teto poderão comercializar seus excedentes, enquanto aquelas que ultrapassarem o limite precisarão adquirir permissões adicionais. Mercado pode ampliar demanda por créditos Estudo da ICC Brasil e da consultoria WayCarbon aponta que o Brasil acumula 148 milhões de toneladas de dióxido de carbono em créditos gerados, com potencial de expansão da demanda de até 530% com a implantação do mercado regulado. Atualmente, o mercado voluntário funciona por meio de contratos entre empresas interessadas em compensar emissões e responsáveis por projetos ambientais, principalmente nas áreas de conservação florestal, reflorestamento e energia. A regulamentação deve ampliar as possibilidades de negociação e conferir maior liquidez aos ativos. A entrada de empresas obrigadas a cumprir metas ambientais também tende a aumentar a procura por esses ativos, hoje adquiridos principalmente por companhias que assumem compromissos voluntários de redução ou compensação de emissões. Investidores acompanham novas oportunidades A regulamentação também estabelece condições para ampliar a presença dos créditos de carbono no mercado financeiro. A Lei nº 15.042/2024 prevê que esses ativos, quando negociados no mercado financeiro e de capitais, sejam considerados valores mobiliários, sujeitos à supervisão da Comissão de Valores Mobiliários (CVM). Fundos de investimento, incluindo os Fundos de Investimento nas Cadeias Produtivas Agroindustriais (Fiagros), estão entre os veículos com potencial para direcionar recursos a projetos ambientais. Apesar das perspectivas de crescimento, especialistas alertam para os riscos envolvidos. Créditos vinculados a projetos ainda em desenvolvimento apresentam maior incerteza, enquanto ativos já certificados oferecem maior previsibilidade, embora possam ter preços mais elevados. O avanço do setor dependerá da definição de regras, da segurança jurídica e da capacidade de atrair compradores e investidores para um mercado sujeito a oscilações de preços e demanda. O cronograma oficial prevê o início das obrigações de relato de emissões em 2027, com a implementação gradual das demais exigências. A negociação plena de cotas está prevista para começar a partir de 2030, com consolidação do sistema em 2031. Na avaliação de especialistas, o novo modelo poderá posicionar o Brasil entre os principais mercados de carbono do mundo, aproveitando o potencial nacional de geração de créditos e atraindo investimentos para iniciativas de descarbonização.

artigo.texto: A SpaceX recebeu autorização da Comissão Federal de Comunicações dos Estados Unidos (FCC) para implantar até 1 milhão de satélites destinados a centros de processamento de dados no espaço. A decisão foi anunciada nesta quarta-feira (25/11) e representa a primeira autorização do tipo concedida pelo órgão americano. O projeto, batizado de Starmind, prevê módulos computacionais em órbita para processar grandes volumes de informações e atender à crescente demanda por capacidade de computação ligada à inteligência artificial. Os satélites funcionarão como data centers orbitais, processando informações que serão utilizadas na Terra. A proposta busca atender à demanda crescente por infraestrutura computacional para sistemas de superinteligência. Segundo a FCC, o projeto deverá cumprir as normas americanas para controle de detritos espaciais. A autorização também prevê sistemas de comunicação de emergência por radiofrequência, usados para monitoramento, rastreamento e controle dos equipamentos em órbita. O presidente da FCC, Brendan Carr, afirmou que o projeto faz parte dos esforços dos Estados Unidos para avançar no desenvolvimento de tecnologias de inteligência artificial. Apesar da autorização, o comunicado não detalha o cronograma de lançamento dos satélites nem quando os centros de dados começarão a operar.

artigo.texto: By Pexcel John Bacon, Reporter THE Philippines should establish transparent carbon market rules and involve workers and affected communities in policymaking to attract private investments while ensuring a fair transition to a low-carbon economy, the International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) said. “If you want the private sector or others to invest in carbon pricing and projects, you need to have a credible and transparent institutions,” IISD Energy Program Director Philip Gass told a joint hearing of the House Committee on Climate Change and the Committee on Sustainable Development Goals on Tuesday. Mr. Gass also urged lawmakers to get communities and workers involved in designing carbon pricing policies, saying their participation would strengthen public support for the system. He said the Philippines could build on existing laws and institutions to develop its carbon pricing system, starting with emissions reporting before introducing a price on carbon. “Report first, apply a price later,” he said, adding that companies and regulators would need time to establish reliable monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) systems. Mr. Gass said MRV standards should be harmonized to the size of emitters. He also raised the need for transparent rules to ensure that carbon credits represent actual and verifiable emissions reductions. Domestic carbon pricing could help the government mobilize funding for climate programs as international climate finance faces growing constraints, he said. “The international system is strained and international climate finance is under stress,” he said. Carbon pricing revenues could be directed toward climate mitigation, adaptation and resilience programs, while also helping cushion households and businesses from the effects of higher energy costs, he added. IISD Senior Policy Advisor Mary Grace Gabis-Reyes said emissions trading systems covered about 25% of global greenhouse gas emissions and generated a record $80 billion in revenues in 2025. Ms. Reyes cited developments in Asian carbon markets, including Japan’s move toward a mandatory emissions trading system and Vietnam’s pilot emissions trading system. In the Philippines, she noted the government has taken steps to develop its carbon market through the adoption of a voluntary forest carbon market roadmap in February, an agreement with Singapore under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement in April, the submission of its third National Determined Contribution (NDC) in September, and the issuance of Executive Order No. 127 in October. The country’s third NDC retained its target to reduce and avoid 75% of projected greenhouse gas emissions from 2025 to 2035, with the unconditional component raised to 7% from 2.71%, Ms. Reyes said. IISD Lead for Carbon Pricing and Philippine Energy Transition Francesse Joy Cordon-Navarro said carbon projects should include clear safeguards for communities, particularly Indigenous Peoples whose ancestral domains may be affected. “Free, prior and informed consent must be explicit and meaningful, and it must take place early on rather than after the principal terms have already been set,” Ms. Navarro said. She said benefit-sharing agreements should specify who is eligible to receive benefits, how much they would receive and when, as well as the remedies available if project developers fail to meet their commitments. IISD Senior Policy Advisor Lorelei S. Astrera said the shift could also affect household energy and transport costs, local businesses and access to essential services. “National gains can exist alongside concentrated local losses,” Ms. Astrera said, calling for policies that anticipate the effects of the transition, protect vulnerable households and give affected groups a voice in decisions on how carbon revenues are spent.

artigo.texto: Vigo County commissioners respond to Sandcut battery storage concerns as project heads to zoning board VIGO COUNTY, Ind. (WTHI) — Vigo County commissioners say they have questioned the developer of a proposed battery storage facility near Sandcut about water, fire safety and the project’s impact on neighbors as the proposal heads toward another public hearing. Commissioners Mark Clinkenbeard and Chris Switzer spoke with News 10 after a commissioners meeting where representatives from NextEra Energy Resources answered questions about Sandcut Storage. Their comments follow a Vigo County Council meeting where residents criticized the way they learned about the proposal and how local officials handled the zoning process. The two commissioners defended that process and said the county’s earlier vote approved rules for battery storage facilities, not the Sandcut project itself. A separate decision on the proposed facility is expected to come before the Area Board of Zoning Appeals. “Now, this particular project will move forward to the BZA, and they will give it an up or down,” Clinkenbeard said. “They may request some more time to get some more answers. I’m not sure.” A hearing on the petition was previously scheduled for Dec. 9 at 10 a.m. at the Vigo County Annex Building. Clinkenbeard encouraged residents to attend. The board could seek additional information rather than make an immediate decision. What’s being proposed? NextEra is proposing a battery energy storage system, or BESS, in the Sandcut area of northern Vigo County. A battery storage facility takes in electricity, stores it and sends it back to the grid later. It does not generate electricity from fuel. The company lists a planned capacity of up to 350 megawatts. That figure describes how quickly the facility could deliver power, not how much energy it could store or how long it could operate at full output. On its Sandcut Storage project page, NextEra estimates a $414 million investment and about 175 construction jobs. The company says the figures are estimates and subject to change, and that the project remains subject to necessary permits and approvals. Clinkenbeard said he believes stored electricity could benefit the local area, though he said the company could not discuss potential contracts. The specific customers and destination of electricity from the project have not been confirmed. Commissioners say they brought community questions to NextEra Switzer said commissioners invited NextEra representatives to address questions they had been receiving from residents. “We just asked a lot of questions that the community’s been asking us for, you know, a couple weeks now,” Switzer said. He said he had hoped more Sandcut residents would attend the commissioners meeting and have an opportunity to hear from the company directly. “We were hoping specifically a few people would be there that’s asked some really tough questions so they could get addressed and kind of have some conversation with NextEra in person,” Switzer said. Clinkenbeard said commissioners spent about half an hour asking questions and encouraged residents to attend the upcoming zoning board hearing. “We invite people to come to that meeting,” he said. “People can come and get some more information.” In News 10’s earlier reporting, several residents said they learned about the proposal from neighbors or social media and wanted more information about its potential effect on their community. “I felt like that we should have known about this and been aware,” longtime Sandcut landowner Mary Vandevender told News 10. She said she had attended a meeting but felt her questions had not been answered. “I’m not going to be okay with this,” Vandevender said. “I’m worried about my land, and I’m worried about my water.” Dustin Houser, who said he learned about the proposal through social media, questioned whether emergency responders would be prepared in the event of a disaster. “My initial concerns are the dangers of this system and that if there’s a disaster, are we prepared for it?” Houser said. Water and fire safety questions Both commissioners said water and fire response were among the subjects they discussed with the developer. Clinkenbeard said he also spoke with Soil and Water about potential water concerns. “We also just had a meeting with Soil and Water, Brendan Kearns, to talk about potential water issues,” Clinkenbeard said. “This facility will not use any water.” Distance from neighbors and screening Clinkenbeard said the developer plans to move the facility farther back from adjoining property owners. He also said vegetation is planned around the site, and commissioners would like to see an additional visual barrier. “They’re going to do, you know, vegetation around the facility, but we would also possibly like to see a berm put around there so that, you know, it’s not visible,” he said. Clinkenbeard also said commissioners asked whether the developer had reached out to nearby property owners about possible land-use agreements. “And they are working on that,” he said. He did not describe the terms of any agreement. Clinkenbeard said the county is trying to balance a landowner’s ability to use their property with the concerns of people living nearby. “We take that all into consideration, because it is important and we want everyone to feel safe,” he said. What the county has — and hasn’t — approved On Nov. 10, commissioners voted 2-1 to approve a countywide zoning change addressing battery storage systems. Switzer and Clinkenbeard voted in favor; Commissioner Mike Morris voted against it. The amendment allows battery storage to be considered as a special exception in specified agricultural, commercial and industrial zoning districts. A special exception requires a separate review. artigo.texto: The insurance industry has spent 2026 arguing about whether it can cover the buildings going up in the global data center build-out. One of the insurers writing that business says the argument may be pointed at the wrong risk. Jarrod Hill (pictured), CEO of CGU and WFI, the broker-facing brands of Insurance Australia Group (IAG), told Insurance Business that warnings about strained capacity do not reflect what underwriters are seeing. "The scale and concentration of data centre investment is changing the risk profile, but it does not mean the market is unable to provide capacity," he said in a written statement. "Globally, the insurance market continues to have significant capacity for well-managed risks, including developments of the scale we are currently seeing in Australia." His response was provided to Insurance Business following the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority's System Risk Outlook published in November 2026, which said the scale of some data center projects is stretching available insurance capacity. Read next: The cost of downtime: Why preparation pays off That debate is about the operators, the companies that build and run these facilities and buy property and business interruption (BI) cover on them. Hill's answer moves to a different exposure. "The key issue is not simply the size of an individual facility, but where that exposure sits and how resilient it is," he said. Where it sits is the point. An operator insures its own building and when that building burns the operator's policy responds. The businesses that rent capacity in it insure nothing there, because they own nothing there. When the facility stops working without being damaged, those customers lose revenue while the only policy covering the site has nothing to pay out on. Hill listed what CGU weighs when it assesses a data center risk: construction, location, natural peril exposure, resilience, redundancy and BI dependencies. That last item is where the capacity debate runs out of road. Capacity answers what happens when a data centre burns down. It does not answer what happens when one simply stops working. Broker Howden put a figure on that distinction in September 2026 in its research on insuring the data centre supercycle. Drawing on the Uptime Institute’s Global Data Center Survey 2025, it found that when outages occur the causes are concentrated and predominantly technical: power, primarily uninterruptible power supply failure, at 45%, cooling at 14%, network at 11% and IT systems at 9%, together accounting for close to four-fifths of impactful events. Only a small proportion involve insured physical damage. Howden’s own conclusion on that risk segment was that outage is where the gap between economic loss and insurability is widest. Half of data centers reported an impactful outage over the past three years, Howden found, with each incident costing an estimated US$0.5 million to US$1 million, implying a global cost of around US$2 billion a year. Conventional BI cover is triggered by physical damage. An outage caused by a power failure, a cooling failure or a cyber attack alone generally does not meet that trigger. Howden identified three reasons outage sits outside the market’s reach: most outages involve no insured physical damage and so fall outside the trigger of a conventional property or BI policy; BI exposure, where cover does respond, is considerable; and outage losses are difficult to model, resting on operators’ contracts, workloads and customer mix rather than physical assets. That is a different claims picture from the fire losses that have shaped data centre experience to date. Read next: Why the simplest alternative risk transfer programs often win The exposure also sits in the wrong place. When a facility goes dark, the loss lands in the dependent business’s own programme rather than the operator’s, and contingent BI wordings typically follow the same damage trigger. Products built for outage do exist. Howden lists non-damage BI alongside service level agreement parametric cover and technology errors and omissions, noting that non-damage BI is available only in some cases, and it is neither standard nor cheap. Where cover does exist, parametric structures are the clearest workaround. A service level agreement breach policy pays a pre-agreed sum when an operator breaches a defined uptime guarantee, with no need to prove physical loss. Howden puts retail colocation and wholesale providers, which carry uptime commitments to large numbers of third-party customers, at roughly 75% of global data centres. Prudential regulators have arrived at the same concern by different routes and reached different conclusions about whose problem it is. None of them addresses who pays. Australia measures the dependency without regulating the provider. Data collected under Prudential Standard CPS 230 Operational Risk Management showed the typical significant insurer identified 28 material service providers. Of the top 100 material service providers reported by APRA-regulated institutions, 80 are headquartered or have their principal operations outside Australia, and some individual providers support institutions that collectively account for more than half of APRA-regulated financial assets. The United Kingdom supervises the providers directly. HM Treasury designated four cloud and technology companies as critical third parties to the UK financial sector under the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026, with effect from 13 July 2026: Amazon Web Services EMEA SARL, Google Cloud EMEA Limited, Microsoft Ireland Operations Limited and Oracle Corporation UK Limited. From that date the Bank of England, the Prudential Regulation Authority and the Financial Conduct Authority have jointly overseen them, with powers to gather information, assess operational resilience, require testing against severe but plausible scenarios and make rules specific to designated providers. artigo.texto: Decreto que regulamenta Redata está pronto e aguarda decisão final de Lula Uma das discussões dentro do governo era a inclusão ou não do gás natural entre as fontes de energia que poderão abastecer os data centers beneficiados pelo novo regime O decreto que regulamenta o Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata) está pronto e aguarda uma decisão final do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), segundo fontes do governo ouvidas pelo Valor. O texto está na Casa Civil e ainda não há previsão para sua publicação. A regulamentação da lei, sancionada em 15 de setembro, deve definir critérios e procedimentos de habilitação das empresas no Redata, a lista de equipamentos elegíveis, os métodos de comprovação das contrapartidas e os parâmetros ambientais e de sustentabilidade. Uma das discussões dentro do governo era a inclusão ou não do gás natural entre as fontes de energia que poderão abastecer os data centers beneficiados pelo novo regime. O Ministério de Minas e Energia (MME) tinha uma posição mais favorável à utilização do insumo durante as discussões, enquanto o Ministério da Fazenda apresentava maior resistência. O Valor apurou que as discussões foram superadas. O texto final aprovado pelo Congresso estabelece que, para usufruir benefícios do Redata, os empreendimentos deverão “atender à totalidade da sua demanda de energia elétrica por meio de contratos de suprimento ou autoprodução proveniente de geração a partir de fontes renováveis ou de baixa emissão, na forma de regulamento”. O tema já havia sido alvo de disputa no Congresso, o que contribuiu para travar a votação. A proposta original do governo previa o uso de fontes “limpas ou renováveis”, mas setores pressionaram para que o combustível, apesar de fóssil, pudesse ser enquadrado entre as fontes elegíveis. Nesta quarta-feira (25), o assessor especial do Ministério da Fazenda, Rafael Dubeux, confirmou a conclusão das negociações entre os ministérios, mas não antecipou o teor da regulamentação. “Está maduro o tema para levar para uma decisão presidencial final”, afirmou após participar do Fórum Dig.ia, em Brasília. Também presente no evento, o ministro das Comunicações, Frederico Siqueira Filho, reforçou que a discussão está na fase final e disse acreditar que nos próximos dias isso será "resolvido", devido à importância do tema. "Vamos assumir esse papel de ser o grande hub de data centers para inteligência artificial e o Brasil será justamente esse local onde a comunidade internacional e os investidores vão realizar seus investimentos." O ministro também mencionou a Política Nacional de Data Centers, que, segundo ele, se somará ao Redata para reduzir burocracias e promover a interação com Estados e Municípios em relação aos licenciamentos. A medida, contudo, ficará para 2027, assim como a política para cabos submarinos. Ao falar sobre a regulamentação durante o evento, o secretário-executivo do Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços (Mdic), Rodrigo Zerbone Loureiro, indicou que há um equilíbrio entre a "vontade ou necessidade" por importação em larga escala de equipamentos para a instalação dos data centers e a proteção e o incentivo à produção nacional. Segundo Loureiro, essa preocupação deverá se refletir na lista de equipamentos contemplados pelos benefícios tributários do Redata. O secretário ressaltou, porém, que a política poderá ser aperfeiçoada a partir de seus resultados e das contribuições do setor produtivo. “Vamos publicar a regulamentação, vai ter uma lista, o setor vai se debruçar, isso vai gerar um impacto, investimentos, reclamações, provavelmente, mas o que mais é preciso é que gere feedback e debate para que a gente consiga, com base em dados, fazer uma avaliação da política e evolução dessa política para patamares superiores de desenvolvimento e investimentos no Brasil", disse. “Em política industrial, a gente não acerta e nem faz parte da pretensão acertar de largada. É tentativa, aprendizado, erro, correção. Isso é feito no mundo inteiro assim e será feito assim”, acrescentou.

artigo.texto: Italy's second auction under MACSE, the storage procurement mechanism that Terna manages, has been completed, and 16 GWh of lithium-ion capacity has been awarded for 2029. That volume has covered the whole of the requirement for the south of the country and for the islands. Some 67 GWh of new projects had qualified for the round, and about 43 GWh of them were offered, which was nearly three times the volume that was needed. The weighted average clearing price was €11,382/MWh-year, which was well below the reserve premium of €27,000/MWh-year and 12% lower than the average of the 2028 auction. South and Calabria have received the largest share, at 9.6 GWh, while Sicily has been given 3 GWh, Central-South 2.8 GWh and Sardinia about 0.5 GWh. Under the method that is used, storage is bought only while the marginal cost of new capacity remains below the saving that it brings in gas-fired generation.
